/-!
# Magic Square value-to-parity relations

This file extracts the elementary probability relations used at the start of
the Magic Square rigidity argument.  A strategy of value at least `1 - ε` has
total rejection mass at most `ε`.  Since the question distribution is
supported on at most 36 directed incidences, the rejection mass at each
incidence is at most `36 * ε`.  This controls malformed answers, consistency
of the two reported bits at every cell, and the parity product on each of the
six row or column constraints.

The arguments apply to arbitrary finite POVMs.  In particular, malformed
answers remain in the event masses when `msBitOrZero` and
`constraintBitOrZero` turn the common answer alphabet into binary outcomes.

## References

The Magic Square game is defined in
`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:512-610`
and blueprint `def:ms-game`.  These relations are the
probabilistic input to the rigidity result cited at paper lines 612-652 from
Coladangelo--Stark, Theorem 6.9.
-/

@[expose] public section

open scoped BigOperators Matrix MatrixOrder ComplexOrder

namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT.MagicSquareRigidity

open LIDT.MIPStarRE.LDT LIDT.MIPStarRE.Quantum

noncomputable section

/-! ## The directed incidence distribution -/

/-- The 36 possible directed constraint-variable incidences. -/
def directedIncidence : ((Fin 6 × Fin 3) × Bool) → _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.MsType × _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.MsType
  | ((i, k), false) => (.constraint i, .var (_root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.msConstraintVars i k))
  | ((i, k), true) => (.var (_root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.msConstraintVars i k), .constraint i)











/-! ## Rejection mass from the game value -/

 instance msWinFalseDecidableRel (x y : _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.MsType) :
    DecidableRel (fun a b : _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.MsAnswer => _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.msWinPredicate x y a b = false) :=
  fun _ _ => inferInstance

private instance msWinTrueDecidableRel (x y : _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.MsType) :
    DecidableRel (fun a b : _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.MsAnswer => _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.msWinPredicate x y a b = true) :=
  fun _ _ => inferInstance

/-- The rejection mass conditioned on a question pair. -/
noncomputable def rejectionMass (S : _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.Strategy _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.msGame) (x y : _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.MsType) : ℝ :=
  @_root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.outcomeEventWeight _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.msGame S x y
    (fun a b => _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.msWinPredicate x y a b = false) (fun _ _ => inferInstance)

/-- The acceptance mass conditioned on a question pair. -/
noncomputable def acceptanceMass (S : _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.Strategy _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.msGame) (x y : _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.MsType) : ℝ :=
  @_root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.outcomeEventWeight _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.msGame S x y
    (fun a b => _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.msWinPredicate x y a b = true) (fun _ _ => inferInstance)

/-- The rejection mass averaged over the Magic Square question distribution. -/
noncomputable def totalRejectionMass (S : _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.Strategy _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.msGame) : ℝ :=
  _root_.LIDT.MIPStarRE.LDT.avgOver (_root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.graphDistribution _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.msEdges _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.msEdges_nonempty) fun xy =>
    _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.MagicSquareRigidity.rejectionMass S xy.1 xy.2



















/-! ## Malformed answers and cell consistency -/

/-- The selected constraint bit, with a wrong-form single-bit answer folded to zero. -/
def constraintBitOrZero (k : Fin 3) : _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.MsAnswer → ZMod 2
  | .triple β => β k
  | .bit _ => 0

/-- Whether an answer has the wrong form for a variable question. -/
def wrongVariableAnswer : _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.MsAnswer → Bool
  | .triple _ => true
  | .bit _ => false

/-- Whether an answer has the wrong form for a constraint question. -/
def wrongConstraintAnswer : _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.MsAnswer → Bool
  | .triple _ => false
  | .bit _ => true

private instance wrongVariableAnswerLeftDecidableRel :
    DecidableRel (fun a _ : _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.MsAnswer => _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.MagicSquareRigidity.wrongVariableAnswer a = true) :=
  fun _ _ => inferInstance

private instance wrongVariableAnswerRightDecidableRel :
    DecidableRel (fun _ b : _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.MsAnswer => _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.MagicSquareRigidity.wrongVariableAnswer b = true) :=
  fun _ _ => inferInstance

private instance wrongConstraintAnswerLeftDecidableRel :
    DecidableRel (fun a _ : _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.MsAnswer => _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.MagicSquareRigidity.wrongConstraintAnswer a = true) :=
  fun _ _ => inferInstance

private instance wrongConstraintAnswerRightDecidableRel :
    DecidableRel (fun _ b : _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.MsAnswer => _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.MagicSquareRigidity.wrongConstraintAnswer b = true) :=
  fun _ _ => inferInstance

 instance forwardCellMismatchDecidableRel (k : Fin 3) :
    DecidableRel (fun a b : _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.MsAnswer => _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.MagicSquareRigidity.constraintBitOrZero k a ≠ _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.msBitOrZero b) :=
  fun _ _ => inferInstance

 instance reverseCellMismatchDecidableRel (k : Fin 3) :
    DecidableRel (fun a b : _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.MsAnswer => _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.msBitOrZero a ≠ _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.MagicSquareRigidity.constraintBitOrZero k b) :=
  fun _ _ => inferInstance

























/-- The forward-incidence mass on which the two totalized cell bits disagree. -/
noncomputable def forwardCellMismatchMass (S : _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.Strategy _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.msGame)
    (i : Fin 6) (k : Fin 3) : ℝ :=
  @_root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.outcomeEventWeight _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.msGame S (.constraint i) (.var (_root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.msConstraintVars i k))
    (fun a b => _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.MagicSquareRigidity.constraintBitOrZero k a ≠ _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.msBitOrZero b) (fun _ _ => inferInstance)

/-- The reverse-incidence mass on which the two totalized cell bits disagree. -/
noncomputable def reverseCellMismatchMass (S : _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.Strategy _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.msGame)
    (i : Fin 6) (k : Fin 3) : ℝ :=
  @_root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.outcomeEventWeight _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.msGame S (.var (_root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.msConstraintVars i k)) (.constraint i)
    (fun a b => _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.msBitOrZero a ≠ _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.MagicSquareRigidity.constraintBitOrZero k b) (fun _ _ => inferInstance)









/-! ## Row and column parity products -/

/-- The real sign `(-1)^b` associated with a binary answer. -/
def bitSign (b : ZMod 2) : ℝ :=
  (-1 : ℝ) ^ b.val







/-- The product of the three output signs, with malformed constraint answers
assigned zero so that they remain parity failures. -/
def constraintParityProduct : _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.MsAnswer → ℝ
  | .triple β => ∏ k : Fin 3, _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.MagicSquareRigidity.bitSign (β k)
  | .bit _ => 0

/-- Failure of the required sign product for one row or column constraint. -/
def ConstraintParityFailure (i : Fin 6) (a : _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.MsAnswer) : Prop :=
  _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.MagicSquareRigidity.constraintParityProduct a ≠ _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.MagicSquareRigidity.bitSign (_root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.msParity i)

private noncomputable instance constraintParityFailureLeftDecidableRel (i : Fin 6) :
    DecidableRel (fun a _ : _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.MsAnswer => _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.MagicSquareRigidity.ConstraintParityFailure i a) :=
  fun a _ => Classical.propDecidable (_root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.MagicSquareRigidity.ConstraintParityFailure i a)

Magic Square answer alphabet. -/

/-- Alice's local failure mass for the row or column sign product. -/

/-!
# Reflections and the state-dependent metric on operators

The self-testing argument for the Magic Square game manipulates `±1`-valued
observables rather than positive operator valued measures.  This file records
the algebra of such observables and the estimates that convert Born masses into
operator bounds.

Postprocessing a projective measurement along a binary relabelling of its
answers produces a *reflection*, that is, a self-adjoint involution; two
reflections coming from one and the same measurement commute, and their product
is the reflection attached to the sum of the two relabellings.  The reflections
of the source are the binary observables of the rest of the development, so this
file uses `MIPStarRE.QPBT.IsBinaryObservable` and its algebra, defined in
`MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Linearity/Defs.lean`, rather than a second predicate of
its own.  Two operators are compared through the norm of the difference of their
actions on a fixed state, the relation `NormCloseOn` below.  That relation is the
unsquared Euclidean distance between `M ψ` and `N ψ`; it is *not* the
state-dependent distance `≈_δ` of the source, which bounds the squared quantity
`⟨ψ|(M - N)ᴴ (M - N)|ψ⟩` and is formalized in this development by `opDistSq`.
The comparison is symmetric, satisfies the triangle inequality, and is unchanged
by multiplication on the left by an isometric operator; `NormCloseOn.opDistSq_le`
converts it into the source's relation.  Finally, a real spectral combination of
the joint effects of the two players has state-dependent norm controlled by the
Born mass of the answer pairs carrying a nonzero coefficient; this is the step
that turns each rejection mass of the value-to-parity layer into an operator
estimate.

## References

The statements supported here are the operator relations in `thm:ms-rigidity`,
blueprint `blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:224-253`, from
`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:612-652`,
proved in Coladangelo--Stark, arXiv:1709.09267v2, Theorem 6.9.
-/

@[expose] public section

open scoped BigOperators Matrix MatrixOrder ComplexOrder

namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT.MagicSquareRigidity

open LIDT.MIPStarRE.LDT LIDT.MIPStarRE.Quantum

noncomputable section

/-! ## Rectangular tensor placement -/

section Kron





/-- Formalization-only: finite sums pass through the first factor. -/
theorem heteroKron_sum_left {ιA ιB γ : Type} [Fintype γ]
    (M : γ → _root_.LIDT.MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op ιA) (N : _root_.LIDT.MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op ιB) :
    _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.heteroKron (∑ c, M c) N = ∑ c, _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.heteroKron (M c) N := by
  ext p q
  simp [_root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.heteroKron, Matrix.kronecker, Matrix.sum_apply, Finset.sum_mul]

/-- Formalization-only: finite sums pass through the second factor. -/
theorem heteroKron_sum_right {ιA ιB γ : Type} [Fintype γ]
    (M : _root_.LIDT.MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op ιA) (N : γ → _root_.LIDT.MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op ιB) :
    _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.heteroKron M (∑ c, N c) = ∑ c, _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.heteroKron M (N c) := by
  ext p q
  simp [_root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.heteroKron, Matrix.kronecker, Matrix.sum_apply, Finset.mul_sum]

end Kron

/-! ## The state-dependent norm -/

section StateNorm

variable {ι : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]

/-- Formalization-only: the action of an operator on a state is homogeneous. -/
theorem applyOperatorToState_smul (c : ℂ) (M : _root_.LIDT.MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op ι) (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι) :
    _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.applyOperatorToState (c • M) ψ = c • _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.applyOperatorToState M ψ := by
  unfold _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.applyOperatorToState
  simp only [map_smul, LinearMap.smul_apply]





/-- An isometric operator preserves the norm of every state. -/
theorem norm_applyOperatorToState_of_isometry {U : _root_.LIDT.MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op ι} (hU : Uᴴ * U = 1)
    (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι) : ‖_root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.applyOperatorToState U ψ‖ = ‖ψ‖ := by
  have h : ‖_root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.applyOperatorToState U ψ‖ ^ 2 = ‖ψ‖ ^ 2 := by
    rw [_root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.MagicSquareRigidity.norm_applyOperatorToState_sq, hU, @norm_sq_eq_re_inner ℂ,
      _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.MagicSquareRigidity.applyOperatorToState_one]
    rfl
  have h1 : (0 : ℝ) ≤ ‖_root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.applyOperatorToState U ψ‖ := norm_nonneg _
  have h2 : (0 : ℝ) ≤ ‖ψ‖ := norm_nonneg _
  nlinarith [h, h1, h2]

/-- Multiplying on the left by an isometric operator does not change the
state-dependent norm. -/
theorem norm_applyOperatorToState_isometry_mul {U : _root_.LIDT.MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op ι} (hU : Uᴴ * U = 1)
    (M : _root_.LIDT.MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op ι) (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι) :
    ‖_root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.applyOperatorToState (U * M) ψ‖ = ‖_root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.applyOperatorToState M ψ‖ := by
  rw [_root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.DistanceCalculus.applyOperatorToState_mul,
    _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.MagicSquareRigidity.norm_applyOperatorToState_of_isometry hU]

end StateNorm

/-! ## Reflections

The *reflections* of `thm:ms-rigidity`, blueprint
`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:228-250`, are the self-adjoint involutions attached to
two-outcome projective measurements, which are exactly the binary observables
`MIPStarRE.QPBT.IsBinaryObservable` of
`MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Linearity/Defs.lean`.  The Magic Square rigidity
argument therefore uses that predicate and its algebra directly:
`IsBinaryObservable.one`, `IsBinaryObservable.mul`,
`IsBinaryObservable.isometry`, `isBinaryObservable_heteroKron_one` and
`isBinaryObservable_one_heteroKron`. -/



/-! ## Closeness in the state-dependent norm -/

/-- Two operators are *close within `δ` on `ψ`* when the state-dependent norm of
their difference is at most `δ`, that is, when the Euclidean distance between
`M ψ` and `N ψ` is at most `δ`.

This is **not** the relation `M ≈_δ N` of `thm:ms-rigidity`, blueprint
`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:249`, paper
`08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:644-646`: there the relation
bounds the *squared* quantity `⟨ψ|(M - N)ᴴ (M - N)|ψ⟩` by `O(δ)`, and it is
formalized in this development by `opDistSq` (`def:povm-distance`, blueprint
`ch12_qpbt_games.tex:219-226`).  The unsquared relation defined here is the one
under which the triangle inequality is additive, which is what the
solution-group computation of `Rigidity/Anticommutation.lean` iterates;
`NormCloseOn.opDistSq_le` converts a bound at scale `δ` here into the bound `δ ^ 2`
for `opDistSq`. -/
def NormCloseOn {ι : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι) (δ : ℝ) (M N : _root_.LIDT.MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op ι) : Prop :=
  ‖_root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.applyOperatorToState (M - N) ψ‖ ≤ δ



/-! ## Sign observables of a projective measurement -/

section SignObs

variable {α d : Type} [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] [Fintype d] [DecidableEq d]

/-- The `±1`-valued observable attached to a measurement together with a binary
relabelling of its answers: an answer labelled `0` carries the eigenvalue `1`
and an answer labelled `1` carries the eigenvalue `-1`.  For the Magic Square
these are the cell observables of `thm:ms-rigidity`, blueprint
`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:224-253`, paper
`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:612-652`. -/
noncomputable def signObs (M : _root_.LIDT.MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement α d) (f : α → ZMod 2) : _root_.LIDT.MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op d :=
  ∑ a, (_root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.MagicSquareRigidity.bitSign (f a) : ℂ) • M.effect a

















end SignObs

/-! ## Deviation of joint spectral combinations on the strategy state -/

section JointDefect







variable {G : _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.Game}

/-- Formalization-only: the joint effects of the two players form a projective
measurement on the composite space when both local measurements are
projective. -/
 noncomputable def jointMeasurement (T : _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.Strategy G) (x : G.QuestionA)
    (y : G.QuestionB) :
    _root_.LIDT.MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement (G.AnswerA × G.AnswerB) (T.ιA × T.ιB) :=
  _root_.LIDT.MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement.ofSumEqOne
    (fun ab => _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.heteroKron ((T.A x).effect ab.1) ((T.B y).effect ab.2))
    (fun ab => _root_.LIDT.MIPStarRE.Quantum.kronecker_nonneg ((T.A x).pos ab.1) ((T.B y).pos ab.2))
    (by
      rw [Fintype.sum_prod_type]
      calc ∑ a : G.AnswerA, ∑ b : G.AnswerB,
            _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.heteroKron ((T.A x).effect a) ((T.B y).effect b)
          = ∑ a : G.AnswerA, _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.heteroKron ((T.A x).effect a)
              (∑ b : G.AnswerB, (T.B y).effect b) := by
            exact Finset.sum_congr rfl fun a _ => (_root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.MagicSquareRigidity.heteroKron_sum_right _ _).symm
        _ = _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.heteroKron (∑ a : G.AnswerA, (T.A x).effect a) (1 : _root_.LIDT.MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op T.ιB) := by
            rw [(T.B y).sum_eq_one, _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.MagicSquareRigidity.heteroKron_sum_left]
        _ = 1 := by rw [(T.A x).sum_eq_one, _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.heteroKron_one_one])











end JointDefect

end

end MIPStarRE.QPBT.MagicSquareRigidity

/-!
# The Magic Square cell relations on the dilated strategy

Every question of the projectively dilated Magic Square strategy carries a
complete projective measurement, so each binary relabelling of its answers
produces a reflection.  Three reflections are attached to a constraint question,
one for each cell of the row or column, and one reflection is attached to each
variable question; the three reflections of a constraint commute exactly and
their product, in any order, is the reflection of the sum of the three reported
bits.  Reflections of the two players commute exactly.

The value-to-parity relations are converted here into operator estimates on the
dilated state, with explicit constants: the six row and column products are
close to the sign prescribed by the corresponding linear equation, and the two
reflections that the two players attach to a common cell are close to each
other.  The two logical Pauli pairs are the reflections at the cells labelled by
the paper's first and fifth variables.

## References

The statement supported here is `thm:ms-rigidity` in
`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:224-253`, from
`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:612-652`,
proved in Coladangelo--Stark, arXiv:1709.09267v2, Theorem 6.9.  The variable and
constraint indices are zero-based, so the paper's first and fifth variables are
the cells `0` and `4`.
-/

@[expose] public section

open scoped BigOperators Matrix MatrixOrder ComplexOrder

namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT.MagicSquareRigidity

open LIDT.MIPStarRE.LDT LIDT.MIPStarRE.Quantum

noncomputable section

/-! ## Deviation of a sign observable from a comparison observable -/







/-! ## Comparison of Born masses with the game error -/







/-! ## The Magic Square reflections of the dilated strategy -/

/-- Alice's cell reflection at one position of a constraint question of the
dilated strategy, placed on its composite space.  This is a pre-isometry
observable of `msDilatedStrategy S`; the state-dependent relations below
evaluate it on `(msDilatedStrategy S).ψ`.  It is not the paper's post-isometry
operator $\tilde A$.  The post-isometry operators on the ideal state in
`thm:ms-rigidity` arise later by conjugating with the local isometries and using
the transfer theorems of issue Dengnifer/MIPStarRE-QPBT-bak#104.  Formalization-only
operator-relation
support for blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:224-253` and paper
`08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:612-652`. -/
noncomputable def msCellObsA (S : _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.Strategy _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.msGame) (i : Fin 6) (k : Fin 3) :
    _root_.LIDT.MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op ((_root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.MagicSquareRigidity.msDilatedStrategy S).ιA × (_root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.MagicSquareRigidity.msDilatedStrategy S).ιB) :=
  _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.heteroKron (_root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.MagicSquareRigidity.signObs ((_root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.MagicSquareRigidity.msDilatedStrategy S).A (_root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.MsType.constraint i))
    (_root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.MagicSquareRigidity.constraintBitOrZero k)) 1

/-- Bob's cell reflection at one position of a constraint question of the
dilated strategy, placed on its composite space.  This is a pre-isometry
observable of `msDilatedStrategy S`; the state-dependent relations below
evaluate it on `(msDilatedStrategy S).ψ`.  It is not the paper's post-isometry
operator $\tilde B$.  The post-isometry operators on the ideal state in
`thm:ms-rigidity` arise later by conjugating with the local isometries and using
the transfer theorems of issue Dengnifer/MIPStarRE-QPBT-bak#104.  Formalization-only
operator-relation
support for blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:224-253` and paper
`08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:612-652`. -/
noncomputable def msCellObsB (S : _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.Strategy _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.msGame) (i : Fin 6) (k : Fin 3) :
    _root_.LIDT.MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op ((_root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.MagicSquareRigidity.msDilatedStrategy S).ιA × (_root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.MagicSquareRigidity.msDilatedStrategy S).ιB) :=
  _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.heteroKron 1 (_root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.MagicSquareRigidity.signObs ((_root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.MagicSquareRigidity.msDilatedStrategy S).B (_root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.MsType.constraint i))
    (_root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.MagicSquareRigidity.constraintBitOrZero k))

/-- Alice's reflection at a variable question of the dilated strategy, placed on
the composite space. -/
noncomputable def msVarObsA (S : _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.Strategy _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.msGame) (j : Fin 9) :
    _root_.LIDT.MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op ((_root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.MagicSquareRigidity.msDilatedStrategy S).ιA × (_root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.MagicSquareRigidity.msDilatedStrategy S).ιB) :=
  _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.heteroKron (_root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.MagicSquareRigidity.signObs ((_root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.MagicSquareRigidity.msDilatedStrategy S).A (_root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.MsType.var j)) _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.msBitOrZero) 1

/-- Bob's reflection at a variable question of the dilated strategy, placed on
the composite space. -/
noncomputable def msVarObsB (S : _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.Strategy _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.msGame) (j : Fin 9) :
    _root_.LIDT.MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op ((_root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.MagicSquareRigidity.msDilatedStrategy S).ιA × (_root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.MagicSquareRigidity.msDilatedStrategy S).ιB) :=
  _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.heteroKron 1 (_root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.MagicSquareRigidity.signObs ((_root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.MagicSquareRigidity.msDilatedStrategy S).B (_root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.MsType.var j)) _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.msBitOrZero)

malformed answers contributing zero. -/

/-!
# Transfer of rigidity bounds along the projective dilation

The self-testing argument behind `thm:ms-rigidity` is carried out for the
projective dilation `msDilatedStrategy S` of an arbitrary Magic Square strategy
`S`.  Its conclusions are state-dependent bounds for the *dilated* projectors,
conjugated by local isometries `φ_A`, `φ_B` out of the enlarged local spaces.
The witness for the original strategy is obtained by composing these isometries
with the ground embeddings, and the operators appearing in its bounds are the
conjugates of the *original* effects, that is, of the compressions `Π P Π` of
the dilated projectors `P` to the ground slice (`Π` the ground projection).

Naimark dilation preserves Born probabilities but not state-dependent `≈_δ`
estimates in general (`references/ldt-paper/orthonormalization.tex:82-101`,
blueprint `ex:easy-but-long`), so `Π P Π` and `P` need not act
alike on the dilated state.  Their difference on the dilated state `ψ'` is the
*leakage* `(1 - Π) P ψ'` of `P` out of the ground slice, and the point of this
file is that in the Magic Square game this leakage is controlled by the
cell-consistency defect of the value-to-parity layer: the dilated effect
`P ⊗ 1` almost agrees with the partner effect `1 ⊗ Q` on the other side, and
`(1 - Π) ⊗ 1` annihilates `1 ⊗ Q ψ'`.  Combined with the closeness of
`(φ_A ⊗ φ_B) ψ'` to the ideal state and the fact that all operators involved
are contractions, this pulls every bound of `thm:ms-rigidity` back from the
dilated strategy to the original one with explicit constants.

## Main statements

* `ms_effect_transfer_A`, `ms_effect_transfer_B`: the bit-measurement distances
  of the original strategy are bounded by three times those of the dilated
  strategy plus `216 ε + 24 η²`, where `η` bounds the state closeness.
* `ms_anticommutator_transfer_A`, `ms_anticommutator_transfer_B`: the
  anticommutator defects transfer with the bound `3 · (dilated) + 15552 ε +
  48 η²`.
* `ms_state_transfer`: the state closeness is unchanged.

## References

blueprint `thm:ms-rigidity`,
paper `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:612-652`.
-/

@[expose] public section

open scoped BigOperators Matrix MatrixOrder ComplexOrder

namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT.MagicSquareRigidity

open LIDT.MIPStarRE.LDT hiding Measurement
open LIDT.MIPStarRE.Quantum MIPStarRE.QPBT.DistanceCalculus

    (b : ZMod 2) : _root_.LIDT.MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op (S.ιA × Option _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.MsAnswer) :=

/-!
# Ancilla isometries for Pauli soundness

Adjoining a unit vector and applying a unitary gives the local isometry in the
final soundness argument. The exact intertwining identity below supplies the
algebraic hypothesis of the range-projection estimates. These results are
recorded in blueprint `thm:pauli-ancilla-intertwining-support`.

## References

Formalization support for blueprint `thm:pauli`, specifically the isometry at
`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1864-1875`.
The registers are ordered as `AA'A''`, with the first two factors grouped.
These constructions do not assume or construct a global polynomial measurement.
-/

@[expose] public section

open scoped BigOperators Matrix MatrixOrder ComplexOrder

namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT

open LIDT.MIPStarRE.Quantum MagicSquareRigidity

noncomputable section

variable {ι κ ν : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
  [Fintype κ] [DecidableEq κ] [Fintype ν] [DecidableEq ν]

/-- Adjoin a unit ancilla on the last two registers, in the extraction order
`(AA')A''`. The norm condition is precisely the normalization of that ancilla. -/
def ancillaBlockIsometry (eta : EuclideanSpace ℂ (κ × ν)) (heta : ‖eta‖ = 1) :
    EuclideanSpace ℂ ι →ₗᵢ[ℂ] EuclideanSpace ℂ ((ι × κ) × ν) where
  toFun psi := _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.reindexState (Equiv.prodAssoc ι κ ν).symm (_root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.vecTensor psi eta)
  map_add' psi chi := by
    ext p
    simp [_root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.reindexState, _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.vecTensor, add_mul]
  map_smul' c psi := by
    ext p
    simp [_root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.reindexState, _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.vecTensor, mul_assoc]
  norm_map' psi := by
    change ‖_root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.reindexState (Equiv.prodAssoc ι κ ν).symm (_root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.vecTensor psi eta)‖ = ‖psi‖
    rw [_root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.reindexState_norm_eq, _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.vecTensor_norm_eq, heta, mul_one]





/-- Apply a matrix isometry after adjoining the unit ancilla. In the source
proof the matrix is the swap unitary and the ancilla is the local EPR state. -/
def unitaryAncillaIsometry (eta : EuclideanSpace ℂ (κ × ν)) (heta : ‖eta‖ = 1)
    (U : _root_.LIDT.MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op ((ι × κ) × ν)) (hU : Uᴴ * U = 1) :
    EuclideanSpace ℂ ι →ₗᵢ[ℂ] EuclideanSpace ℂ ((ι × κ) × ν) where
  toLinearMap := (Matrix.toEuclideanLin U).comp
    (_root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.ancillaBlockIsometry eta heta).toLinearMap
  norm_map' psi := by
    change ‖Matrix.toEuclideanLin U (_root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.ancillaBlockIsometry eta heta psi)‖ = ‖psi‖
    rw [_root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.MagicSquareRigidity.norm_toEuclideanLin_of_conjTranspose_mul_eq_one hU, LinearIsometry.norm_map]





end

end MIPStarRE.QPBT

/-!
# Public helpers for the upstream LIDT interface

These finite-sum and measurement lemmas support the QPBT without modifying its LIDT dependency.
The marginal-state construction and rank-zero argument adapt the private proofs in
`LionSR/MIPStarRE`, commit `f382c801026f53a9efc260fdee707cb35e0adb15`, module
`MIPStarRE.LDT.MakingMeasurementsProjective.LocalityPreservingRepair`.
The remaining lemmas are QPBT extensions of the upstream measurement and distribution APIs.
Their proofs use the public definitions and Mathlib finite-dimensional linear algebra.
-/

@[expose] public section

open scoped BigOperators MatrixOrder Matrix ComplexOrder

namespace LIDT
namespace MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement
variable {d : Type*} [Fintype d] [DecidableEq d]
variable {α β : Type*} [Fintype α] [Fintype β]

/-- A complete measurement is determined by its effects. -/
theorem ext {M N : _root_.LIDT.MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement α d} (h : ∀ a, M.effect a = N.effect a) :
    M = N := by
  cases M with
  | mk M hM =>
      cases N with
      | mk N hN =>
          cases M with
          | mk effectM posM leM =>
              cases N with
              | mk effectN posN leN =>
                  simp only at h
                  have heffect : effectM = effectN := funext h
                  subst effectN
                  rfl



end MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement
end LIDT

namespace LIDT
namespace MIPStarRE.LDT

/-- Averaging scalar multiples of a fixed operator averages their coefficients
over the distribution's support. -/
theorem averageOperatorOverDistribution_smul_const {α ι : Type*}
    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] (𝒟 : _root_.LIDT.MIPStarRE.LDT.Distribution α) (c : α → ℂ)
    (A : _root_.LIDT.MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op ι) :
    _root_.LIDT.MIPStarRE.LDT.averageOperatorOverDistribution 𝒟 (fun a => c a • A) =
      (∑ a ∈ 𝒟.support, (𝒟.weight a : ℂ) * c a) • A := by
  simp only [_root_.LIDT.MIPStarRE.LDT.averageOperatorOverDistribution, Finset.sum_smul]
  apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
  intro a ha
  rw [← Complex.real_smul, smul_assoc]



namespace Distribution.IsProbability

/-- A probability distribution has total weight one over any finite superset
of its explicit support. -/
theorem weight_sum_eq_one_of_subset {α : Type*}
    {𝒟 : _root_.LIDT.MIPStarRE.LDT.Distribution α} (h𝒟 : 𝒟.IsProbability) {s : Finset α}
    (hsubset : 𝒟.support ⊆ s) :
    ∑ a ∈ s, 𝒟.weight a = 1 := by
  have hsum :
      ∑ a ∈ 𝒟.support, 𝒟.weight a = ∑ a ∈ s, 𝒟.weight a :=
    Finset.sum_subset hsubset (fun a _ ha => 𝒟.outsideSupport a ha)
  exact hsum ▸ h𝒟.weight_sum_eq_one

end Distribution.IsProbability
end MIPStarRE.LDT
end LIDT

namespace LIDT
namespace MIPStarRE.LDT.Preliminaries

variable {p : ℕ} [Fact p.Prime]
variable {F : Type*} [Field F] [Fintype F] [DecidableEq F] [Algebra (ZMod p) F]
variable {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]

/-- Fourier orthogonality for the canonical character over an arbitrary finite
coordinate type. This is the finite-index reindexing of
`prop:fourier-fact-vector`. -/
theorem expect_ffChar_sum_mul (v : ι → F) :
    𝔼 u : (ι → F), _root_.LIDT.MIPStarRE.LDT.Preliminaries.ffChar (p := p) (F := F) (∑ i, u i * v i) =
      if v = 0 then (1 : ℂ) else 0 := by
  let eι : ι ≃ Fin (Fintype.card ι) := Fintype.equivFin ι
  let reindex : (ι → F) ≃ (Fin (Fintype.card ι) → F) :=
    { toFun := fun u j => u (eι.symm j)
      invFun := fun u i => u (eι i)
      left_inv := fun u => by
        funext i
        simp
      right_inv := fun u => by
        funext j
        simp }
  let v' : Fin (Fintype.card ι) → F := reindex v
  calc
    𝔼 u : (ι → F), _root_.LIDT.MIPStarRE.LDT.Preliminaries.ffChar (p := p) (F := F) (∑ i, u i * v i) =
        𝔼 u : (Fin (Fintype.card ι) → F),
          _root_.LIDT.MIPStarRE.LDT.Preliminaries.ffVecChar (p := p) (F := F) v' u := by
      refine Finset.expect_equiv reindex (by simp) ?_
      intro u _
      rw [_root_.LIDT.MIPStarRE.LDT.Preliminaries.ffVecChar_apply]
      congr 2
      exact Fintype.sum_equiv eι
        (fun i => u i * v i)
        (fun j => reindex u j * v' j)
        (fun i => by simp [reindex, v'])
    _ = if v' = 0 then (1 : ℂ) else 0 := _root_.LIDT.MIPStarRE.LDT.Preliminaries.fourier_fact_vector v'
    _ = if v = 0 then (1 : ℂ) else 0 := by
      have reindex_zero : reindex (0 : ι → F) = 0 := by
        ext j
        rfl
      by_cases hv : v = 0
      · subst v
        rw [show v' = 0 by exact reindex_zero]
        simp
      · have hv' : v' ≠ 0 := by
          intro hv'
          apply hv
          apply reindex.injective
          rw [reindex_zero]
          exact hv'
        simp [hv, hv']

/-- Sum form of canonical-character orthogonality over an arbitrary finite
coordinate type. -/
theorem sum_ffChar_sum_mul (v : ι → F) :
    ∑ u : ι → F, _root_.LIDT.MIPStarRE.LDT.Preliminaries.ffChar (p := p) (F := F) (∑ i, u i * v i) =
      if v = 0 then (Fintype.card (ι → F) : ℂ) else 0 := by
  rw [← Fintype.card_smul_expect, _root_.LIDT.MIPStarRE.LDT.Preliminaries.expect_ffChar_sum_mul]
  by_cases hv : v = 0 <;> simp [hv]

end MIPStarRE.LDT.Preliminaries
end LIDT

namespace LIDT
namespace MIPStarRE.LDT.MakingMeasurementsProjective
open LIDT.MIPStarRE.LDT
noncomputable section

/-- The diagonal block of a bipartite operator at a fixed right index. -/
def diagBlock {ιA ιB : Type*}
    [Fintype ιA] [DecidableEq ιA] [Fintype ιB] [DecidableEq ιB]
    (M : _root_.LIDT.MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op (ιA × ιB)) (b : ιB) :
    _root_.LIDT.MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op ιA :=
  M.submatrix (fun i => (i, b)) (fun j => (j, b))

/-- The normalized left marginal of a bipartite density, obtained by
averaging its diagonal right blocks. -/
def leftMarginalDensity {ιA ιB : Type*}
    [Fintype ιA] [DecidableEq ιA] [Fintype ιB] [DecidableEq ιB] [Nonempty ιB]
    (ρ : _root_.LIDT.MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op (ιA × ιB)) : _root_.LIDT.MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op ιA :=
  ((((Fintype.card ιB : _root_.LIDT.MIPStarRE.LDT.Error) : _root_.LIDT.MIPStarRE.LDT.Error)⁻¹ : _root_.LIDT.MIPStarRE.LDT.Error) : ℂ) •
    ∑ b : ιB, _root_.LIDT.MIPStarRE.LDT.MakingMeasurementsProjective.diagBlock ρ b

/-- Positivity passes from a bipartite density to its left marginal. -/
private lemma leftMarginalDensity_nonneg {ιA ιB : Type*}
    [Fintype ιA] [DecidableEq ιA] [Fintype ιB] [DecidableEq ιB] [Nonempty ιB]
    {ρ : _root_.LIDT.MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op (ιA × ιB)} (hρ : 0 ≤ ρ) :
    0 ≤ _root_.LIDT.MIPStarRE.LDT.MakingMeasurementsProjective.leftMarginalDensity ρ := by
  have hρpsd : ρ.PosSemidef := Matrix.nonneg_iff_posSemidef.mp hρ
  have hsum : 0 ≤ ∑ b : ιB, _root_.LIDT.MIPStarRE.LDT.MakingMeasurementsProjective.diagBlock ρ b := by
    refine Finset.sum_nonneg fun b _ => ?_
    refine Matrix.nonneg_iff_posSemidef.mpr ?_
    simpa [_root_.LIDT.MIPStarRE.LDT.MakingMeasurementsProjective.diagBlock] using hρpsd.submatrix (fun i => (i, b))
  have hcoeff : 0 ≤ ((((Fintype.card ιB : _root_.LIDT.MIPStarRE.LDT.Error) : _root_.LIDT.MIPStarRE.LDT.Error)⁻¹ : _root_.LIDT.MIPStarRE.LDT.Error) : ℂ) := by
    positivity
  simpa [_root_.LIDT.MIPStarRE.LDT.MakingMeasurementsProjective.leftMarginalDensity] using smul_nonneg hcoeff hsum

/-- The local state on the left factor defined by the left marginal density
of a bipartite state. This formalization-only definition supports the
locality-preserving projectivization lemma and the explicit-constant form of
the orthonormalization lemma. -/
def leftMarginalState {ιA ιB : Type*}
    [Fintype ιA] [DecidableEq ιA] [Fintype ιB] [DecidableEq ιB] [Nonempty ιB]
    (ψ : _root_.LIDT.MIPStarRE.LDT.QuantumState (ιA × ιB)) : _root_.LIDT.MIPStarRE.LDT.QuantumState ιA where
  density := _root_.LIDT.MIPStarRE.LDT.MakingMeasurementsProjective.leftMarginalDensity ψ.density
  density_psd := by
    exact leftMarginalDensity_nonneg ψ.density_psd















end

/-!
# Generalized Pauli operators and EPR states

The definitions here use finite matrix entries and rank-one projectors, so they
are usable by the later game statements without introducing an abstract
operator algebra.  The observable/projector expansions are obtained from
finite-field Fourier orthogonality in characteristic two.

## References

The source-facing nodes are blueprint `def:lin-reg`, `def:EPR`,
`def:generalized-pauli`, and `lem:pauli-observable-expansion`.  The paper origin is
`references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:908-1161`.
-/

@[expose] public section

open scoped BigOperators Matrix ComplexOrder

namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT

open LIDT.MIPStarRE.Quantum
open LIDT.MIPStarRE.LDT.Preliminaries

variable {K : Type*} [Field K] [Fintype K] [DecidableEq K]
  [Algebra (ZMod 2) K]

/-- The two generalized Pauli bases used by the test in blueprint
`def:generalized-pauli`, paper origin
`references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:1052-1096`.
-/
inductive PauliKind where
  | X
  | Z
  deriving DecidableEq, Repr, Inhabited
instance PauliKind.instFintype : Fintype _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.PauliKind :=
  ⟨{.X, .Z}, by intro x; cases x <;> simp⟩
/-- The binary character used for generalized Pauli phases; see
`references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:1052-1081`.

It is public because the Fourier expansion declarations below expose this
character in their statement types. -/
noncomputable def phaseSign (t : ZMod 2) : ℂ :=
  if t = 0 then 1 else -1

/-- Formalization-only expansion of a sum over the binary field into its two
terms. -/
theorem sum_zmod_two {M : Type*} [AddCommMonoid M] (f : ZMod 2 → M) :
    ∑ b, f b = f 0 + f 1 := by
  calc
    ∑ b, f b = ∑ i : Fin 2, f (ZMod.finEquiv 2 i) := by
      exact Fintype.sum_equiv (ZMod.finEquiv 2).symm f
        (fun i : Fin 2 => f (ZMod.finEquiv 2 i)) (fun _ => rfl)
    _ = f (ZMod.finEquiv 2 0) + f (ZMod.finEquiv 2 1) := Fin.sum_univ_two _
    _ = f 0 + f 1 := by rfl

/-- Formalization-only case split for the binary field: every element is zero
or one. -/
theorem zmod_two_eq_zero_or_one (b : ZMod 2) : b = 0 ∨ b = 1 := by
  by_cases hb : b = 0
  · exact Or.inl hb
  · right
    have hval_ne : b.val ≠ 0 := (ZMod.val_ne_zero b).mpr hb
    have hval_lt : b.val < 2 := ZMod.val_lt b
    have hval : b.val = 1 := by omega
    exact (ZMod.val_eq_one (by omega) b).mp hval

/-- In characteristic two, the standard additive character is the sign
character used by the binary Pauli definitions. -/
theorem phaseSign_eq_ffChar (t : ZMod 2) :
    _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.phaseSign t = ZMod.stdAddChar (N := 2) t := by
  by_cases ht : t = 0
  · subst t
    rw [_root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.phaseSign, if_pos rfl]
    exact (ZMod.stdAddChar (N := 2)).map_zero_eq_one.symm
  · have hval : t.val = 1 := by
      have hval_ne : t.val ≠ 0 := (ZMod.val_ne_zero t).mpr ht
      have hval_lt : t.val < 2 := ZMod.val_lt t
      omega
    have ht_one : t = 1 := (ZMod.val_eq_one (by omega) t).mp hval
    subst t
    rw [_root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.phaseSign, if_neg one_ne_zero]
    change (-1 : ℂ) = ZMod.stdAddChar (N := 2) ((1 : ℤ) : ZMod 2)
    rw [ZMod.stdAddChar_coe]
    convert Complex.exp_pi_mul_I.symm using 1
    all_goals ring_nf

/-- The binary sign character carries a sum to the product of the two signs.
This is the character property underlying blueprint
`def:generalized-pauli`, paper origin
`references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:1052-1096`. -/
theorem phaseSign_add (s t : ZMod 2) :
    _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.phaseSign (s + t) = _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.phaseSign s * _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.phaseSign t := by
  rw [_root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.phaseSign_eq_ffChar, _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.phaseSign_eq_ffChar, _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.phaseSign_eq_ffChar]
  exact (ZMod.stdAddChar (N := 2)).map_add_eq_mul s t

/-- The binary sign character takes real values, so conjugation fixes it. It is
used by the observable expansions of blueprint
`def:generalized-pauli`, paper origin
`references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:1052-1096`. -/
theorem star_phaseSign (t : ZMod 2) : star (_root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.phaseSign t) = _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.phaseSign t := by
  by_cases ht : t = 0 <;> simp [_root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.phaseSign, ht]



/-- The binary sign character sends sums to products. -/
theorem phaseSign_sum {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] (f : ι → ZMod 2) :
    _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.phaseSign (∑ i, f i) = ∏ i, _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.phaseSign (f i) := by
  classical
  induction (Finset.univ : Finset ι) using Finset.induction_on with
  | empty => simp [_root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.phaseSign]
  | @insert i s hi ih =>
      rw [Finset.sum_insert hi, Finset.prod_insert hi, _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.phaseSign_add, ih]

omit [Fintype K] [DecidableEq K] in
/-- The product of the coordinate phases is the phase of the trace pairing. -/
theorem prod_phaseSign_binTrace_dotProduct {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι]
    (u v : ι → K) :
    ∏ i, _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.phaseSign (_root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.binTrace K (u i * v i)) =
      _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.phaseSign (_root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.binTrace K (dotProduct u v)) := by
  rw [← _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.phaseSign_sum]
  congr 2
  simp [dotProduct]

/-- The complex amplitude `(√n)⁻¹` normalizing a uniform superposition over `n`
basis vectors squares to `n⁻¹`.

This formalization-only normalization identity supports the Pauli normalizer
of blueprint `def:EPR`, paper origin
`references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:908-950`, and the seed-fiber and
correlated-ancilla amplitudes of the direct low-degree transport. -/
theorem inv_sqrt_natCast_mul_self (n : ℕ) :
    (Real.sqrt (n : ℝ) : ℂ)⁻¹ * (Real.sqrt (n : ℝ) : ℂ)⁻¹ =
      (n : ℂ)⁻¹ := by
  calc
    (Real.sqrt (n : ℝ) : ℂ)⁻¹ * (Real.sqrt (n : ℝ) : ℂ)⁻¹ =
        ((Real.sqrt (n : ℝ) : ℂ) ^ 2)⁻¹ := by
      rw [pow_two, mul_inv_rev]
    _ = ((n : ℝ) : ℂ)⁻¹ := by
      rw [← Complex.ofReal_pow, Real.sq_sqrt (Nat.cast_nonneg n)]
    _ = (n : ℂ)⁻¹ := by norm_num



omit [Field K] [DecidableEq K] [Algebra (ZMod 2) K] in
private theorem pauliNormalizer_mul_self {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι]
    [DecidableEq ι] :
    (∏ _i : ι, (Real.sqrt (Fintype.card K : ℝ) : ℂ)⁻¹) *
        (∏ _i : ι, (Real.sqrt (Fintype.card K : ℝ) : ℂ)⁻¹) =
      (Fintype.card (ι → K) : ℂ)⁻¹ := by
  simp only [Finset.prod_const, Finset.card_univ]
  rw [← mul_pow, _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.inv_sqrt_natCast_mul_self, inv_pow, Fintype.card_fun]
  norm_cast

omit [Fintype K] [DecidableEq K] in
 theorem phaseSign_binTrace_dotProduct_add {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι]
    (u v w : ι → K) :
    _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.phaseSign (_root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.binTrace K (dotProduct u v)) *
        _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.phaseSign (_root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.binTrace K (dotProduct u w)) =
      _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.phaseSign (_root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.binTrace K (dotProduct u (v + w))) := by
  rw [← _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.phaseSign_add]
  congr 2
  simp [dotProduct, mul_add, Finset.sum_add_distrib]

omit [Fintype K] [DecidableEq K] in
 theorem add_add_eq_zero_iff_eq_add {ι : Type*} (a x y : ι → K) :
    a + (x + y) = 0 ↔ x = y + a := by
  letI : CharP K 2 :=
    (Algebra.charP_iff (ZMod 2) K 2).mp (ZMod.charP 2)
  constructor
  · intro h
    funext i
    have hi : a i + (x i + y i) = 0 := by
      simpa only [Pi.add_apply, Pi.zero_apply] using congrFun h i
    have hax : a i + x i = y i := (CharTwo.add_eq_zero).mp (by
      simpa only [add_assoc] using hi)
    calc
      x i = a i + (a i + x i) := (CharTwo.add_cancel_left (a i) (x i)).symm
      _ = a i + y i := by rw [hax]
      _ = y i + a i := add_comm _ _
  · intro h
    funext i
    have hxi : x i = y i + a i := by
      simpa only [Pi.add_apply] using congrFun h i
    simp only [Pi.add_apply, Pi.zero_apply, hxi]
    calc
      a i + (y i + a i + y i) = (a i + a i) + (y i + y i) := by abel
      _ = 0 := by rw [CharTwo.add_self_eq_zero, CharTwo.add_self_eq_zero, zero_add]

 theorem sum_phaseSign_dotProduct {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι]
    [DecidableEq ι] (v : ι → K) :
    ∑ u : ι → K, _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.phaseSign (_root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.binTrace K (dotProduct u v)) =
      if v = 0 then (Fintype.card (ι → K) : ℂ) else 0 := by
  calc
    ∑ u : ι → K, _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.phaseSign (_root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.binTrace K (dotProduct u v)) =
        ∑ u : ι → K, _root_.LIDT.MIPStarRE.LDT.Preliminaries.ffChar (p := 2) (F := K) (dotProduct u v) := by
      apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
      intro u _
      rw [_root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.phaseSign_eq_ffChar]
      rfl
    _ = if v = 0 then (Fintype.card (ι → K) : ℂ) else 0 := by
      simpa only [dotProduct] using
        (_root_.LIDT.MIPStarRE.LDT.Preliminaries.sum_ffChar_sum_mul (p := 2) (F := K) (ι := ι) v)

/--
The shift operator `τ^X(a)`.  Blueprint `def:generalized-pauli`; paper origin
`references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:1052-1096`.
-/
noncomputable def tauShift (a : K) : _root_.LIDT.MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op K :=
  fun i j => if i = j + a then 1 else 0

/--
The phase operator `τ^Z(b)`, with the fixed binary trace in the phase.  It is
the second operator of blueprint `def:generalized-pauli`; paper
`references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:1052-1096`.
-/
noncomputable def tauPhase (b : K) : _root_.LIDT.MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op K :=
  fun i j => if i = j then _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.phaseSign (_root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.binTrace K (b * j)) else 0

/-- The binary shift Pauli operator is Hermitian.  This is a
formalization-only specialization of the generalized Pauli definition. -/
theorem binaryTauShift_conjTranspose :
    (_root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.tauShift (K := ZMod 2) 1)ᴴ = _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.tauShift (K := ZMod 2) 1 := by
  ext i j
  have hiff : j = i + 1 ↔ i = j + 1 := by
    rw [CharTwo.eq_add_iff_add_eq, eq_comm]
  simp [_root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.tauShift, Matrix.conjTranspose_apply, hiff]

/-- The binary phase Pauli operator is Hermitian.  This is a
formalization-only specialization of the generalized Pauli definition. -/
theorem binaryTauPhase_conjTranspose :
    (_root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.tauPhase (K := ZMod 2) 1)ᴴ = _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.tauPhase (K := ZMod 2) 1 := by
  ext i j
  rcases _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.zmod_two_eq_zero_or_one i with rfl | rfl <;>
    rcases _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.zmod_two_eq_zero_or_one j with rfl | rfl <;>
      norm_num [_root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.tauPhase, _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.phaseSign, Matrix.conjTranspose_apply,
        Algebra.trace_self_apply]

/-- The binary shift Pauli operator is symmetric.  This formalization-only
identity supports transport across an EPR state. -/
theorem binaryTauShift_transpose :
    (_root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.tauShift (K := ZMod 2) 1)ᵀ = _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.tauShift (K := ZMod 2) 1 := by
  ext i j
  have hiff : j = i + 1 ↔ i = j + 1 := by
    rw [CharTwo.eq_add_iff_add_eq, eq_comm]
  simp [_root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.tauShift, Matrix.transpose_apply, hiff]

/-- The binary phase Pauli operator is symmetric.  This formalization-only
identity supports transport across an EPR state. -/
theorem binaryTauPhase_transpose :
    (_root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.tauPhase (K := ZMod 2) 1)ᵀ = _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.tauPhase (K := ZMod 2) 1 := by
  ext i j
  rcases _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.zmod_two_eq_zero_or_one i with rfl | rfl <;>
    rcases _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.zmod_two_eq_zero_or_one j with rfl | rfl <;>
      norm_num [_root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.tauPhase, _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.phaseSign, Matrix.transpose_apply,
        Algebra.trace_self_apply]

/-- The binary shift Pauli operator squares to the identity.  This is a
formalization-only specialization of the generalized Pauli definition. -/
theorem binaryTauShift_sq :
    _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.tauShift (K := ZMod 2) 1 * _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.tauShift (K := ZMod 2) 1 = 1 := by
  ext i j
  simp only [Matrix.mul_apply]
  rw [_root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.sum_zmod_two]
  rcases _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.zmod_two_eq_zero_or_one i with rfl | rfl <;>
    rcases _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.zmod_two_eq_zero_or_one j with rfl | rfl <;>
      simp +decide [_root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.tauShift]

/-- The binary phase Pauli operator squares to the identity.  This is a
formalization-only specialization of the generalized Pauli definition. -/
theorem binaryTauPhase_sq :
    _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.tauPhase (K := ZMod 2) 1 * _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.tauPhase (K := ZMod 2) 1 = 1 := by
  ext i j
  simp only [Matrix.mul_apply]
  rw [_root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.sum_zmod_two]
  rcases _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.zmod_two_eq_zero_or_one i with rfl | rfl <;>
    rcases _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.zmod_two_eq_zero_or_one j with rfl | rfl <;>
      norm_num [_root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.tauPhase, _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.phaseSign, Matrix.one_apply, Algebra.trace_self_apply]

/-- The binary shift and phase Pauli operators anticommute.  This is a
formalization-only specialization of their generalized definitions. -/
theorem binaryTauShift_mul_tauPhase :
    _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.tauShift (K := ZMod 2) 1 * _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.tauPhase (K := ZMod 2) 1 =
      -(_root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.tauPhase (K := ZMod 2) 1 * _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.tauShift (K := ZMod 2) 1) := by
  ext i j
  change
    (∑ k, _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.tauShift (K := ZMod 2) 1 i k * _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.tauPhase (K := ZMod 2) 1 k j) =
      -(∑ k, _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.tauPhase (K := ZMod 2) 1 i k * _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.tauShift (K := ZMod 2) 1 k j)
  rw [_root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.sum_zmod_two, _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.sum_zmod_two]
  rcases _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.zmod_two_eq_zero_or_one i with rfl | rfl <;>
    rcases _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.zmod_two_eq_zero_or_one j with rfl | rfl <;>
      simp +decide [_root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.tauShift, _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.tauPhase, _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.phaseSign]

/-- The single-qudit eigenvector coordinate used in the tensor-product basis;
see `references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:1126-1161`. -/
noncomputable def singlePauliVec (W : _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.PauliKind) (e x : K) : ℂ :=
  match W with
  | .Z => if x = e then 1 else 0
  | .X =>
      (Real.sqrt (Fintype.card K : ℝ) : ℂ)⁻¹ * _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.phaseSign (_root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.binTrace K (e * x))

/--
The normalized single/multi-qudit eigenvector for a Pauli basis label.  For an
index type `ι`, the input `e : ι → K` labels the tensor-product basis vector.
This is the vector form of blueprint
`def:generalized-pauli`, paper origin
`references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:1101-1122`.
-/
noncomputable def pauliVec {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    (W : _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.PauliKind) (e : ι → K) (x : ι → K) : ℂ :=
  ∏ i : ι, _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.singlePauliVec W (e i) (x i)

/--
The rank-one projector onto `pauliVec W e`.  This is the projective measurement
element `τ^W_e` in blueprint `def:generalized-pauli`; paper
`references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:1101-1122`.
-/
noncomputable def pauliProj {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    (W : _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.PauliKind) (e : ι → K) : _root_.LIDT.MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op (ι → K) :=
  Matrix.vecMulVec (_root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.pauliVec W e) (fun x => star (_root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.pauliVec W e x))

private theorem pauliProj_X_apply {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    (e x y : ι → K) :
    _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.pauliProj .X e x y =
      (Fintype.card (ι → K) : ℂ)⁻¹ *
        _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.phaseSign (_root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.binTrace K (dotProduct e (x + y))) := by
  change
    (∏ i : ι, (Real.sqrt (Fintype.card K : ℝ) : ℂ)⁻¹ *
        _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.phaseSign (_root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.binTrace K (e i * x i))) *
      star (∏ i : ι, (Real.sqrt (Fintype.card K : ℝ) : ℂ)⁻¹ *
        _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.phaseSign (_root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.binTrace K (e i * y i))) = _
  rw [Finset.prod_mul_distrib, Finset.prod_mul_distrib,
    _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.prod_phaseSign_binTrace_dotProduct, _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.prod_phaseSign_binTrace_dotProduct]
  simp only [star_mul, _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.star_phaseSign]
  have hstar :
      star (∏ _i : ι, (Real.sqrt (Fintype.card K : ℝ) : ℂ)⁻¹) =
        ∏ _i : ι, (Real.sqrt (Fintype.card K : ℝ) : ℂ)⁻¹ := by
    simp
  rw [hstar]
  calc
    (∏ _i : ι, (Real.sqrt (Fintype.card K : ℝ) : ℂ)⁻¹) *
          _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.phaseSign (_root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.binTrace K (dotProduct e x)) *
        (_root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.phaseSign (_root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.binTrace K (dotProduct e y)) *
          ∏ _i : ι, (Real.sqrt (Fintype.card K : ℝ) : ℂ)⁻¹) =
        ((∏ _i : ι, (Real.sqrt (Fintype.card K : ℝ) : ℂ)⁻¹) *
          ∏ _i : ι, (Real.sqrt (Fintype.card K : ℝ) : ℂ)⁻¹) *
            (_root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.phaseSign (_root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.binTrace K (dotProduct e x)) *
              _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.phaseSign (_root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.binTrace K (dotProduct e y))) := by ring
    _ = _ := by
      rw [pauliNormalizer_mul_self, phaseSign_binTrace_dotProduct_add]

/-- Generalized Pauli eigenspace projectors are symmetric matrices in
characteristic two. For the `X` basis this uses `x + y = y + x` in the
character formula; for the `Z` basis the projector is diagonal. This is the
EPR-transport property used in `lem:qld-comm-cons`, paper
`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:455-465`. -/
theorem pauliProj_transpose {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    (W : _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.PauliKind) (e : ι → K) :
    (_root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.pauliProj W e)ᵀ = _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.pauliProj W e := by
  ext x y
  rw [Matrix.transpose_apply]
  cases W with
  | X =>
      rw [pauliProj_X_apply, pauliProj_X_apply, add_comm]
  | Z =>
      have hreal (z : ι → K) : star (_root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.pauliVec .Z e z) = _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.pauliVec .Z e z := by
        simp [_root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.pauliVec, _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.singlePauliVec]
      change _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.pauliVec .Z e y * star (_root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.pauliVec .Z e x) =
        _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.pauliVec .Z e x * star (_root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.pauliVec .Z e y)
      rw [hreal x, hreal y, mul_comm]

/-- Generalized Pauli eigenspace projectors are mutually orthogonal. This is

theorem pauliProj_mul_pauliProj {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    (W : _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.PauliKind) (e f : ι → K) :
    _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.pauliProj W e * _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.pauliProj W f =
      if e = f then _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.pauliProj W e else 0 := by
  classical
  ext x z
  cases W with
  | X =>
      rw [Matrix.mul_apply]
      simp_rw [pauliProj_X_apply]
      have hsum :
          (∑ y : ι → K,
              ((Fintype.card (ι → K) : ℂ)⁻¹ *
                  _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.phaseSign (_root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.binTrace K (dotProduct e (x + y)))) *
                ((Fintype.card (ι → K) : ℂ)⁻¹ *
                  _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.phaseSign (_root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.binTrace K (dotProduct f (y + z))))) =
            (Fintype.card (ι → K) : ℂ)⁻¹ *
                (Fintype.card (ι → K) : ℂ)⁻¹ *
              _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.phaseSign (_root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.binTrace K (dotProduct e x)) *
              _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.phaseSign (_root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.binTrace K (dotProduct f z)) *
              ∑ y : ι → K,
                _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.phaseSign (_root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.binTrace K (dotProduct y (e + f))) := by
        rw [Finset.mul_sum]
        apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
        intro y _
        rw [← phaseSign_binTrace_dotProduct_add e x y,
          ← phaseSign_binTrace_dotProduct_add f y z,
          ← phaseSign_binTrace_dotProduct_add y e f,
          dotProduct_comm e y, dotProduct_comm f y]
        ring
      rw [hsum, sum_phaseSign_dotProduct]
      letI : CharP K 2 :=
        (Algebra.charP_iff (ZMod 2) K 2).mp (ZMod.charP 2)
      by_cases hef : e = f
      · subst f
        have hzero : e + e = 0 := by
          funext i
          exact CharTwo.add_self_eq_zero (e i)
        rw [if_pos rfl, if_pos hzero]
        rw [pauliProj_X_apply]
        have hcard : (Fintype.card (ι → K) : ℂ) ≠ 0 := by positivity
        field_simp
        rw [← phaseSign_binTrace_dotProduct_add e x z]
      · have hadd : e + f ≠ 0 := by
          intro h
          apply hef
          funext i
          exact CharTwo.add_eq_zero.mp (congrFun h i)

      have hz (g y : ι → K) :
          _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.pauliVec .Z g y = if y = g then 1 else 0 := by
        simp [_root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.pauliVec, _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.singlePauliVec, Fintype.prod_ite_zero, ← funext_iff]

      · subst f
        simp [_root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.pauliProj, Matrix.mul_apply, Matrix.vecMulVec_apply, hz]
      · have hfe : f ≠ e := Ne.symm hef
        simp [_root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.pauliProj, Matrix.mul_apply, Matrix.vecMulVec_apply, hz, hef, hfe]

/-- A compact operator-valued form of a generalized Pauli observable from
blueprint `def:generalized-pauli`, paper origin
`references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:1052-1096`.
-/
noncomputable def tauObservable {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    (W : _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.PauliKind) (a : ι → K) : _root_.LIDT.MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op (ι → K) :=
  fun x y =>
    ∏ i : ι,
      match W with
      | .X => _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.tauShift (a i) (x i) (y i)
      | .Z => _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.tauPhase (a i) (x i) (y i)

/--
The EPR vector on a finite label space.  Blueprint `def:EPR`; paper origin
`references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:946-955`.
-/
noncomputable def eprState (V : Type*) [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V] [Nonempty V] :
    EuclideanSpace ℂ (V × V) :=
  (EuclideanSpace.equiv (V × V) ℂ).symm
    (fun p : V × V =>
      if p.1 = p.2 then (Real.sqrt (Fintype.card V : ℝ) : ℂ)⁻¹ else 0)

/-- The EPR vector is normalized on a nonempty finite carrier; see
`def:EPR`, `references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:946-955`. -/
theorem eprState_norm (V : Type*) [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V] [Nonempty V] :
    ‖_root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.eprState V‖ = 1 := by
  apply (sq_eq_sq₀ (norm_nonneg _) zero_le_one).mp
  rw [EuclideanSpace.norm_sq_eq]
  change
    (∑ p : V × V,
      ‖if p.1 = p.2 then (Real.sqrt (Fintype.card V : ℝ) : ℂ)⁻¹ else 0‖ ^ 2) =
      1 ^ 2
  rw [Fintype.sum_prod_type]
  have hcard : 0 < (Fintype.card V : ℝ) := by positivity
  calc
    ∑ x : V, ∑ y : V,
        ‖if x = y then (Real.sqrt (Fintype.card V : ℝ) : ℂ)⁻¹ else 0‖ ^ 2 =
        ∑ _x : V, ‖(Real.sqrt (Fintype.card V : ℝ) : ℂ)⁻¹‖ ^ 2 := by
      apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
      intro x _
      rw [Finset.sum_eq_single x]
      · simp
      · intro y _ hy
        simp [hy.symm]
      · simp
    _ = 1 := by
      rw [Finset.sum_const, nsmul_eq_mul]
      simp only [norm_inv, Complex.norm_real, Real.norm_eq_abs,
        abs_of_nonneg (Real.sqrt_nonneg _)]
      rw [inv_pow, Real.sq_sqrt hcard.le]
      norm_num [hcard.ne']
    _ = 1 ^ 2 := by norm_num

/--
Fourier expansion of a generalized Pauli observable in the Pauli projectors.
This theorem is the characteristic-two (binary) specialization of the forward
identity `eq:pauli-obs-proj` in `lem:pauli-observable-expansion`,
with blueprint source `lem:pauli-observable-expansion`; paper origin
`references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:1151-1161`.

**Scope restriction:** This characteristic-two specialization is separated
from the general-prime identity as documented in
`docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_characteristic-two-pauli-scope.tex`.
-/
theorem tauObservable_eq_sum_pauliProj {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    (W : _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.PauliKind) (a : ι → K) :
    _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.tauObservable W a =
      ∑ e : ι → K, _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.phaseSign (_root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.binTrace K (dotProduct a e)) • _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.pauliProj W e := by
  ext x y
  rw [show
    (∑ e : ι → K, _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.phaseSign (_root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.binTrace K (dotProduct a e)) • _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.pauliProj W e) x y =
      ∑ e : ι → K,
        _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.phaseSign (_root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.binTrace K (dotProduct a e)) * _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.pauliProj W e x y by
          rw [Matrix.sum_apply]
          rfl]
  cases W with
  | X =>
      change
        (∏ i : ι, if x i = y i + a i then 1 else 0) =
          ∑ e : ι → K,
            _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.phaseSign (_root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.binTrace K (dotProduct a e)) * _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.pauliProj .X e x y
      simp_rw [pauliProj_X_apply]
      rw [Fintype.prod_boole]
      have hsupport : (∀ i, x i = y i + a i) ↔ x = y + a := by
        simpa only [Pi.add_apply] using
          (funext_iff (f := x) (g := y + a)).symm
      simp only [hsupport]
      have hsum :
          (∑ e : ι → K,
            _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.phaseSign (_root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.binTrace K (dotProduct a e)) *
              ((Fintype.card (ι → K) : ℂ)⁻¹ *
                _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.phaseSign (_root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.binTrace K (dotProduct e (x + y))))) =
            (Fintype.card (ι → K) : ℂ)⁻¹ *
              ∑ e : ι → K,
                _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.phaseSign (_root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.binTrace K (dotProduct e (a + (x + y)))) := by
        rw [Finset.mul_sum]
        apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
        intro e _
        calc
          _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.phaseSign (_root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.binTrace K (dotProduct a e)) *
                ((Fintype.card (ι → K) : ℂ)⁻¹ *
                  _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.phaseSign (_root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.binTrace K (dotProduct e (x + y)))) =
              (Fintype.card (ι → K) : ℂ)⁻¹ *
                (_root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.phaseSign (_root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.binTrace K (dotProduct e a)) *
                  _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.phaseSign (_root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.binTrace K (dotProduct e (x + y)))) := by
            rw [dotProduct_comm a e]
            ring
          _ = _ := by rw [phaseSign_binTrace_dotProduct_add]
      rw [hsum, sum_phaseSign_dotProduct]
      by_cases hsupport : x = y + a
      · have hzero : a + (x + y) = 0 :=
          (add_add_eq_zero_iff_eq_add a x y).mpr hsupport
        rw [if_pos hsupport, if_pos hzero]
        exact (inv_mul_cancel₀
          (show (Fintype.card (ι → K) : ℂ) ≠ 0 by positivity)).symm
      · have hzero : a + (x + y) ≠ 0 := fun h =>
          hsupport ((add_add_eq_zero_iff_eq_add a x y).mp h)
        simp [hsupport, hzero]
  | Z =>
      change
        (∏ i : ι, if x i = y i then _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.phaseSign (_root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.binTrace K (a i * y i)) else 0) =
          ∑ e : ι → K, _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.phaseSign (_root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.binTrace K (dotProduct a e)) *
            ((∏ i : ι, if x i = e i then 1 else 0) *
              star (∏ i : ι, if y i = e i then 1 else 0))
      simp only [Fintype.prod_ite_zero, Finset.prod_const_one]
      by_cases hxy : x = y
      · subst y
        rw [_root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.prod_phaseSign_binTrace_dotProduct]
        simp [← funext_iff]
      · simp [← funext_iff, hxy]

/-- Formalization-only: a product of coordinate indicators is the indicator of
equality of the two tuples. -/
private theorem prod_indicator_eq_one_apply {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι]
    (x y : ι → K) :
    (∏ _i : ι, (if x _i = y _i then (1 : ℂ) else 0)) = if x = y then 1 else 0 := by
  by_cases h : x = y
  · subst h
    simp
  · rw [if_neg h]
    obtain ⟨i, hi⟩ := Function.ne_iff.mp h
    exact Finset.prod_eq_zero (Finset.mem_univ i) (if_neg hi)

/-- The generalized Pauli observable at the zero label is the identity, for
either Pauli kind.  blueprint
`def:generalized-pauli`. -/
theorem tauObservable_zero {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] (W : _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.PauliKind) :
    _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.tauObservable (K := K) W (0 : ι → K) = 1 := by
  ext x y
  rw [Matrix.one_apply, ← prod_indicator_eq_one_apply (K := K) x y]
  simp only [_root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.tauObservable]
  cases W <;>
    exact Finset.prod_congr rfl fun i _ => by
      simp [_root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.tauShift, _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.tauPhase, _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.phaseSign]

/-- The Pauli basis projectors of one kind sum to the identity: they are the
effects of a complete measurement.  This is the Fourier expansion
`tauObservable_eq_sum_pauliProj` of `lem:pauli-observable-expansion` at the zero
label, blueprint `lem:pauli-observable-expansion`, paper
`references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:1151-1161`. -/
theorem sum_pauliProj_eq_one {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] (W : _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.PauliKind) :
    (∑ e : ι → K, _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.pauliProj W e) = 1 := by
  have h := _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.tauObservable_eq_sum_pauliProj (K := K) W (0 : ι → K)
  rw [_root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.tauObservable_zero] at h
  rw [h]
  refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun e _ => ?_
  have hzero : dotProduct (0 : ι → K) e = 0 := by
    simp [dotProduct]
  rw [hzero]
  simp [_root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.phaseSign]

/-- Each Pauli basis projector is positive semidefinite: it is the rank-one
outer product of the normalized Pauli eigenvector with itself. -/
theorem posSemidef_pauliProj {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    (W : _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.PauliKind) (e : ι → K) : (_root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.pauliProj W e).PosSemidef := by
  set A : Matrix Unit (ι → K) ℂ :=
    Matrix.of (fun (_ : Unit) (x : ι → K) => star (_root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.pauliVec W e x)) with hA
  have h : _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.pauliProj W e = Aᴴ * A := by
    ext x y
    rw [Matrix.mul_apply]
    simp [hA, _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.pauliProj, Matrix.vecMulVec_apply, Matrix.conjTranspose_apply]
  rw [h]
  exact Matrix.posSemidef_conjTranspose_mul_self A

end MIPStarRE.QPBT
