/-!
# The Pauli basis test

This file supplies the finite question and answer alphabets, the typed
conditionally-linear question sampler, and the Boolean win predicate for the
Pauli basis test.  The quantitative soundness theorem is isolated in
`Soundness.lean`.

## References

The source-facing nodes are blueprint `def:admissible`,
`def:pauli-question-distribution`, and `def:pauli-win-predicate`; their paper origin is
`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:908-1225`.
-/

@[expose] public section

open scoped BigOperators

namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT

open LIDT.MIPStarRE.LDT

noncomputable section

/-- The numerical admissible Pauli-test parameter tuple.  Its scalar carrier
uses the once-and-for-all model `fixedFieldModel q hq`, so the paper's fixed
self-dual-normal identification is not quantified in the test statement.  This
is blueprint
`def:admissible`, paper origin
`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:958-961`.
-/
structure AdmissibleParams where
  q : ℕ
  m : ℕ
  d : ℕ
  hd : 1 ≤ d
  hq : _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.IsAdmissibleSize q
  hdvd : m ∣ q

/-- Every admissible parameter tuple has positive ambient dimension. This
follows from positivity of the admissible field size and the divisibility
`P.m ∣ P.q` in `def:admissible`, blueprint
`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex`, paper origin
`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:958-961`.
-/
theorem AdmissibleParams.one_le_m (P : _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.AdmissibleParams) : 1 ≤ P.m := by
  have hqpos : 0 < P.q := by
    rcases P.hq with ⟨k, _, hq⟩
    rw [hq]
    exact Nat.pow_pos (by decide)
  exact Nat.one_le_iff_ne_zero.mpr
    (ne_zero_of_dvd_ne_zero (Nat.ne_of_gt hqpos) P.hdvd)

/-- The fixed scalar model of an admissible parameter tuple.  It is a
compatibility view of the global `fixedFieldModel` selector, not an independently
quantified field representation.  This is the field representation of
`def:admissible`, blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex`; paper
origin `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:958-961`.
-/
@[reducible] noncomputable def AdmissibleParams.model
    (P : _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.AdmissibleParams) : _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.FixedFieldModel P.q :=
  _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.fixedFieldModel P.q P.hq

/-- The low-degree parameter tuple determined by an admissible Pauli-test
tuple.  It is not an additional hypothesis of `thm:pauli`.  The low-degree
parameters are those of `def:ld-game`, blueprint
`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex`, paper origin
`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:958-961`.
-/
@[reducible] def AdmissibleParams.toLdParams (P : _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.AdmissibleParams) : _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.LdParams where
  q := P.q
  m := P.m
  d := P.d
  k := 1
  hm := P.one_le_m
  hd := P.hd
  hk := by decide
  hq := P.hq
  hdvd := P.hdvd

/-- The scalar carrier associated with an admissible parameter tuple.  It is
the globally fixed field carrier selected by `AdmissibleParams.model` in
blueprint
`def:admissible`, paper origin
`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:958-961`.
-/
abbrev PauliScalar (P : _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.AdmissibleParams) := P.model.K

/-- The six families of Pauli-test questions.  This is part of
blueprint `def:pauli-question-distribution`,
paper origin `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:964-1120`.
-/
inductive PauliType where
  | point (W : _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.PauliKind)
  | aline (W : _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.PauliKind)
  | dline (W : _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.PauliKind)
  | pauli (W : _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.PauliKind)
  | pairW (W : _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.PauliKind)
  | pair
  | ms (t : _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.MsType)
  deriving DecidableEq, Repr, Inhabited, Fintype

/-- The register blocks used by the Pauli question space.  These are the
coordinates displayed in blueprint
`def:pauli-question-distribution`, paper origin
`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:964-1120`.
-/
abbrev PauliIndex (P : _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.AdmissibleParams) :=
  (((((Fin P.m ⊕ Fin P.m) ⊕ Unit) ⊕ Fin P.m) ⊕ Unit) ⊕ Unit)

/-- The ambient Pauli question coefficient space (blueprint
`def:pauli-question-distribution`; paper origin
`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:964-1120`).
-/
abbrev PauliSpace (P : _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.AdmissibleParams) := _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.PauliIndex P → _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.PauliScalar P

/-- The coefficient register indexed by the Boolean cube in
blueprint `def:generalized-pauli`, paper origin
`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:908-945`.
-/
abbrev PauliRegister (P : _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.AdmissibleParams) := _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.Cube P.m → _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.PauliScalar P

/- The nested sum is the fixed register order
`V_X ⊕ V_Z ⊕ V_I ⊕ V_V ⊕ V_{R_X} ⊕ V_{R_Z}` from the blueprint. -/
/-- The `V_X` block of an ambient Pauli vector (blueprint
`def:pauli-question-distribution`; paper origin
`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:964-1120`). -/
def pauliXBlock {P : _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.AdmissibleParams} (z : _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.PauliSpace P) : Fin P.m → _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.PauliScalar P :=
  fun i => z (.inl (.inl (.inl (.inl (.inl i)))))

/-- The `V_Z` block of an ambient Pauli vector in blueprint
`def:pauli-question-distribution`, paper origin
`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:964-1120`.
-/
def pauliZBlock {P : _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.AdmissibleParams} (z : _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.PauliSpace P) : Fin P.m → _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.PauliScalar P :=
  fun i => z (.inl (.inl (.inl (.inl (.inr i)))))

/-- The scalar block `V_I` of an ambient Pauli vector in
blueprint `def:pauli-question-distribution`,
paper origin `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:964-1120`.
-/
def pauliScalarBlock {P : _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.AdmissibleParams} (z : _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.PauliSpace P) : _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.PauliScalar P :=
  z (.inl (.inl (.inl (.inr ()))))

/-- The direction block `V_V` of an ambient Pauli vector in
blueprint `def:pauli-question-distribution`,
paper origin `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:964-1120`.
-/
def pauliDirectionBlock {P : _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.AdmissibleParams} (z : _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.PauliSpace P) : Fin P.m → _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.PauliScalar P :=
  fun i => z (.inl (.inl (.inr i)))

/-- The `r_X` scalar block in the Pauli question content from
blueprint `def:pauli-question-distribution`,
paper origin `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:964-1120`.
-/
def pauliRXBlock {P : _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.AdmissibleParams} (z : _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.PauliSpace P) : _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.PauliScalar P :=
  z (.inl (.inr ()))

/-- The `r_Z` scalar block in the Pauli question content from
blueprint `def:pauli-question-distribution`,
paper origin `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:964-1120`.
-/
def pauliRZBlock {P : _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.AdmissibleParams} (z : _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.PauliSpace P) : _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.PauliScalar P :=
  z (.inr ())

/-- Select the basis-dependent point block from a Pauli question content in
blueprint `def:pauli-question-distribution`,
paper origin `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:964-1120`.
-/
def pauliPointBlock {P : _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.AdmissibleParams} (W : _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.PauliKind) (z : _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.PauliSpace P) :
    Fin P.m → _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.PauliScalar P :=
  match W with
  | .X => _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.pauliXBlock z
  | .Z => _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.pauliZBlock z

/-- Read the low-degree register selected by a basis from an ambient Pauli
vector.  This is restriction to the basis-selected registers of
`def:pauli-question-distribution`, blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex`, paper origin
`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:964-1120`.
-/
def pauliToLd (P : _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.AdmissibleParams) (W : _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.PauliKind) (z : _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.PauliSpace P) :
    _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.LdSpace P.toLdParams :=
  fun i => match i with
  | .inl (.inl j) => _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.pauliPointBlock W z j
  | .inl (.inr _) => _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.pauliScalarBlock z
  | .inr j => _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.pauliDirectionBlock z j

/-- Embed a low-degree vector into the basis-selected Pauli blocks, clearing the
other basis and the two `r` registers.  This is extension into the
basis-selected registers of `def:pauli-question-distribution`, blueprint
`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex`, paper origin
`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:964-1120`.
-/
def embedLd (P : _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.AdmissibleParams) (W : _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.PauliKind)
    (u : _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.LdSpace P.toLdParams) : _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.PauliSpace P :=
  fun i => match i with
  | .inl (.inl (.inl (.inl (.inl j)))) =>
      match W with
      | .X => u (.inl (.inl j))
      | .Z => 0
  | .inl (.inl (.inl (.inl (.inr j)))) =>
      match W with
      | .X => 0
      | .Z => u (.inl (.inl j))
  | .inl (.inl (.inl (.inr _))) => u (.inl (.inr ()))
  | .inl (.inl (.inr j)) => u (.inr j)
  | .inl (.inr _) => 0
  | .inr _ => 0

/-- The type-4 projection retaining `V_X`, `V_Z`, `V_{R_X}`, and `V_{R_Z}` from
blueprint `def:pauli-question-distribution`, paper
origin `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:964-1120`.
-/
def pauliSharedProjection {P : _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.AdmissibleParams} (z : _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.PauliSpace P) : _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.PauliSpace P :=
  fun i => match i with
  | .inl (.inl (.inl (.inl (.inl j)))) => z (.inl (.inl (.inl (.inl (.inl j)))))
  | .inl (.inl (.inl (.inl (.inr j)))) => z (.inl (.inl (.inl (.inl (.inr j)))))
  | .inl (.inl (.inl (.inr _))) => 0
  | .inl (.inl (.inr _)) => 0
  | .inl (.inr _) => z (.inl (.inr ()))
  | .inr _ => z (.inr ())



/-- The conditionally linear map attached to each Pauli question type.  The
point and line maps are the corresponding
low-degree maps embedded in the selected basis block; Pair, Magic Square, and
Pair/W types use the shared projection; Pauli/W is the zero-level map.  This
is the direct finite-space form of blueprint
`def:pauli-question-distribution`, paper origin
`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:964-1120`.
-/
noncomputable def pauliCL (P : _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.AdmissibleParams) (t : _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.PauliType) :
    _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.PauliSpace P → _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.PauliSpace P :=
  match t with
  | .point W => fun z => _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.embedLd P W (_root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.ldPointCL P.toLdParams (_root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.pauliToLd P W z))
  | .aline W => fun z => _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.embedLd P W (_root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.ldALineCL P.toLdParams (_root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.pauliToLd P W z))
  | .dline W => fun z => _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.embedLd P W (_root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.ldDLineCL P.toLdParams (_root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.pauliToLd P W z))
  | .pauli _ => fun _ => 0
  | .pairW _ => _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.pauliSharedProjection
  | .pair => _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.pauliSharedProjection
  | .ms _ => _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.pauliSharedProjection

















/-- A finite edge set for the typed Pauli question graph.  The self-loops and
the displayed type-incidence families are the graph used by the sampler in
blueprint `def:pauli-question-distribution`, paper origin
`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:964-1120`.
-/
def pauliEdges : Finset (Sym2 _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.PauliType) :=
  let loops := Finset.univ.image (fun t : _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.PauliType => Sym2.mk t t)
  let lineEdges :=
    (Finset.univ : Finset _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.PauliKind).image (fun W =>
      Sym2.mk (.point W) (.aline W)) ∪
      (Finset.univ : Finset _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.PauliKind).image (fun W =>
        Sym2.mk (.point W) (.dline W)) ∪
      (Finset.univ : Finset _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.PauliKind).image (fun W =>
        Sym2.mk (.point W) (.pauli W))
  let basisEdges :=
    (Finset.univ : Finset _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.PauliKind).image (fun W =>
      Sym2.mk (.point W) (.pairW W)) ∪
      ({Sym2.mk (.point .X) (.ms (.var ⟨0, by decide⟩)),
        Sym2.mk (.point .Z) (.ms (.var ⟨4, by decide⟩))} : Finset (Sym2 _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.PauliType))
  let pairEdges :=
    (Finset.univ : Finset _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.PauliKind).image (fun W =>
      Sym2.mk (.pairW W) .pair)
  let msEdges' :=
    (Finset.univ : Finset (_root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.MsType × _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.MsType)).filter (fun xy =>
      Sym2.mk xy.1 xy.2 ∈ _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.msEdges) |>.image (fun xy =>
        Sym2.mk (.ms xy.1) (.ms xy.2))
  loops ∪ lineEdges ∪ basisEdges ∪ pairEdges ∪ msEdges'

/-- A Pauli question is a type together with a full ambient coefficient vector
(blueprint `def:pauli-question-distribution`; paper
origin `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:964-1120`).
-/
abbrev PauliQuestion (P : _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.AdmissibleParams) := _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.PauliType × _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.PauliSpace P

/-- The Pauli question carrying no additional coefficient data, as in
blueprint `def:pauli-win-predicate`, paper origin
`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1006-1008`.
Its ambient coefficient vector is zero. -/
def pauliQuestion (P : _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.AdmissibleParams) (W : _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.PauliKind) : _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.PauliQuestion P :=
  (.pauli W, 0)

/-- The ordered-edge subtype used by the Pauli question sampler.  This is
the finite carrier underlying `graphDistribution pauliEdges`, used to state
`def:pauli-question-distribution`, blueprint
`ch13_qpbt_test.tex`, paper origin
`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:964-1120`.
-/
abbrev PauliEdge :=
  {e : _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.PauliType × _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.PauliType // Sym2.mk e.1 e.2 ∈ _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.pauliEdges}

/-- The Pauli graph has a loop, so its ordered-edge subtype is nonempty.  This
is a finite-carrier fact used only to instantiate the uniform source sampler
for `def:pauli-question-distribution`; the graph itself is the source-facing
object `pauliEdges` above (same blueprint and paper references).
-/
theorem pauliEdge_nonempty : Nonempty _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.PauliEdge := by
  refine ⟨⟨(.point .X, .point .X), ?_⟩⟩
  simp [_root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.pauliEdges]



/-- The Pauli question distribution from blueprint
`def:pauli-question-distribution`, paper origin
`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1070-1120`.
-/
noncomputable def pauliQuestionDistribution (P : _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.AdmissibleParams) :
    _root_.LIDT.MIPStarRE.LDT.Distribution (_root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.PauliQuestion P × _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.PauliQuestion P) :=
  by
    classical
    letI : Nonempty _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.PauliEdge := _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.pauliEdge_nonempty
    exact
      _root_.LIDT.MIPStarRE.LDT.Distribution.map
        (_root_.LIDT.MIPStarRE.LDT.uniformDistribution (_root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.PauliEdge × _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.PauliSpace P))
        (fun s =>
          ((s.1.1.1, _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.pauliCL P s.1.1.1 s.2),
            (s.1.1.2, _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.pauliCL P s.1.1.2 s.2)))

/-- The finite answer alphabet for the Pauli basis test.  Its constructors are
the seven answer forms in blueprint `def:pauli-win-predicate`,
paper origin `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1126-1225`.
-/
inductive PauliAnswer (P : _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.AdmissibleParams) where
  | value (a : _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.PauliScalar P)
  | alinePoly (a : Fin (P.d + 1) → _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.PauliScalar P)
  | dlinePoly (a : Fin (P.m * P.d + 1) → _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.PauliScalar P)
  | pairBits (a : ZMod 2 × ZMod 2)
  | bit (a : ZMod 2)
  | msTriple (a : Fin 3 → ZMod 2)
  | pauliOutcome (a : _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.PauliRegister P)
  deriving DecidableEq

/-- A formalization-only total relabeling from the global Pauli-test answer
alphabet to a Pauli register. It folds wrong-form answers into zero so that a
Pauli question yields a complete `PauliRegister`-indexed measurement. -/
def pauliAnswerOrZero {P : _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.AdmissibleParams} : _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.PauliAnswer P → _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.PauliRegister P
  | .pauliOutcome u => u
  | _ => 0

/-- A finite sum code used only to construct the `Fintype` instance for the
answer alphabet in blueprint
`def:pauli-win-predicate`, paper origin
`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1126-1225`.
-/
abbrev PauliAnswerCode (P : _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.AdmissibleParams) :=
  _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.PauliScalar P ⊕
    ((Fin (P.d + 1) → _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.PauliScalar P) ⊕
      ((Fin (P.m * P.d + 1) → _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.PauliScalar P) ⊕
        ((ZMod 2 × ZMod 2) ⊕
          (ZMod 2 ⊕ ((Fin 3 → ZMod 2) ⊕ _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.PauliRegister P)))))

/-- The constructor-preserving finite-code equivalence for `PauliAnswer`.  It
is the finite encoding used to state `def:pauli-win-predicate`, blueprint
`ch13_qpbt_test.tex`, paper origin
`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1126-1225`.
-/
noncomputable def pauliAnswerEquiv (P : _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.AdmissibleParams) :
    _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.PauliAnswer P ≃ _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.PauliAnswerCode P where
  toFun
    | .value a => .inl a
    | .alinePoly a => .inr (.inl a)
    | .dlinePoly a => .inr (.inr (.inl a))
    | .pairBits a => .inr (.inr (.inr (.inl a)))
    | .bit a => .inr (.inr (.inr (.inr (.inl a))))
    | .msTriple a => .inr (.inr (.inr (.inr (.inr (.inl a)))))
    | .pauliOutcome a => .inr (.inr (.inr (.inr (.inr (.inr a)))))
  invFun
    | .inl a => .value a
    | .inr (.inl a) => .alinePoly a
    | .inr (.inr (.inl a)) => .dlinePoly a
    | .inr (.inr (.inr (.inl a))) => .pairBits a
    | .inr (.inr (.inr (.inr (.inl a)))) => .bit a
    | .inr (.inr (.inr (.inr (.inr (.inl a))))) => .msTriple a
    | .inr (.inr (.inr (.inr (.inr (.inr a))))) => .pauliOutcome a
  left_inv := by
    intro x
    cases x <;> rfl
  right_inv := by
    intro x
    cases x with
    | inl a => rfl
    | inr x =>
        cases x with
        | inl a => rfl
        | inr x =>
            cases x with
            | inl a => rfl
            | inr x =>
                cases x with
                | inl a => rfl
                | inr x =>
                    cases x with
                    | inl a => rfl
                    | inr x =>
                        cases x with
                        | inl a => rfl
                        | inr a => rfl

noncomputable instance instFintypePauliAnswer (P : _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.AdmissibleParams) : Fintype (_root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.PauliAnswer P) :=
  Fintype.ofEquiv (_root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.PauliAnswerCode P) (_root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.pauliAnswerEquiv P).symm

instance instInhabitedPauliAnswer (P : _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.AdmissibleParams) : Inhabited (_root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.PauliAnswer P) :=
  ⟨.bit 0⟩

/-- The phase bit `γ(u_X,u_Z,r_X,r_Z)` from `eq:gamma-value`.  It uses the
fixed trace selected by `P.model`, as required by the paper's fixed
self-dual-normal representation.  Blueprint
`eq:gamma-value`; paper origin
`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1198-1212`.
-/
noncomputable def gammaValue (P : _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.AdmissibleParams)
    (uX uZ : Fin P.m → _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.PauliScalar P)
    (rX rZ : _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.PauliScalar P) : ZMod 2 :=
  _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.fixedBinTrace P.model
    (dotProduct (rX • _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.indicatorVec uX) (rZ • _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.indicatorVec uZ))

/-- The commutation bit attached to a full Pauli ambient question, from
`eq:gamma-value` in blueprint
`def:pauli-win-predicate`, paper origin
`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1198-1212`.
-/
noncomputable def pauliPairGamma (P : _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.AdmissibleParams) (z : _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.PauliSpace P) : ZMod 2 :=
  _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.gammaValue P (_root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.pauliXBlock z) (_root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.pauliZBlock z)
    (_root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.pauliRXBlock z) (_root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.pauliRZBlock z)

/-- The answer constructor prescribed by each Pauli question type; this is the
well-formedness part of blueprint
`def:pauli-win-predicate`, paper origin
`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1126-1225`.
-/
def validPauliAnswer {P : _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.AdmissibleParams} (t : _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.PauliType) (a : _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.PauliAnswer P) : Bool :=
  match t, a with
  | .point _, .value _ => true
  | .aline _, .alinePoly _ => true
  | .dline _, .dlinePoly _ => true
  | .pauli _, .pauliOutcome _ => true
  | .pairW _, .bit _ => true
  | .pair, .pairBits _ => true
  | .ms (.constraint _), .msTriple _ => true
  | .ms (.var _), .bit _ => true
  | _, _ => false

/-- The axis-line versus point relation used by blueprint
`def:pauli-win-predicate`, paper origin
`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1126-1225`.
-/
def pauliAlinePointCondition (P : _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.AdmissibleParams) (W : _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.PauliKind)
    (line point : _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.PauliSpace P) (f : Fin (P.d + 1) → _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.PauliScalar P)
    (a : _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.PauliScalar P) : Prop :=
  -- The universal form preserves the source's zero-direction convention.
  ∀ t : _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.PauliScalar P,
    _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.pauliPointBlock W point =
        _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.pauliPointBlock W line + t • _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.coordinateDirection
          (_root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.chiIndex P.toLdParams (_root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.pauliScalarBlock line)) →
      _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.evalCoefficient f t = a

/-- The diagonal-line versus point relation used by blueprint
`def:pauli-win-predicate`, paper origin
`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1126-1225`.
-/
def pauliDlinePointCondition (P : _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.AdmissibleParams) (W : _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.PauliKind)
    (line point : _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.PauliSpace P) (f : Fin (P.m * P.d + 1) → _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.PauliScalar P)
    (a : _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.PauliScalar P) : Prop :=
  ∀ t : _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.PauliScalar P,
    _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.pauliPointBlock W point = _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.pauliPointBlock W line +
        t • _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.pauliDirectionBlock line →
      _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.evalCoefficient f t = a

/-- The raw Pauli-versus-point consistency relation from blueprint
`def:pauli-win-predicate`, paper origin
`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1126-1225`.
-/
def pauliPointPauliCondition (P : _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.AdmissibleParams) (W : _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.PauliKind)
    (point : _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.PauliSpace P) (h : _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.PauliRegister P) (a : _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.PauliScalar P) : Prop :=
  _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.lowDegreeEnc h (_root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.pauliPointBlock W point) = a

/-- The Pair/W consistency relation, including the one-sided gamma gate, from
blueprint `def:pauli-win-predicate`, paper origin
`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1126-1225`.
-/
def pauliPairCondition (P : _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.AdmissibleParams) (W : _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.PauliKind)
    (z : _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.PauliSpace P) (β : ZMod 2) (bits : ZMod 2 × ZMod 2) : Prop :=
  _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.pauliPairGamma P z ≠ 0 ∨
    (match W with
    | .X => bits.1 = β
    | .Z => bits.2 = β)

/-- The point/Pair/W trace consistency relation from blueprint
`def:pauli-win-predicate`, paper origin
`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1126-1225`.
-/
def pauliPointPairCondition (P : _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.AdmissibleParams) (W : _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.PauliKind)
    (z : _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.PauliSpace P) (a : _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.PauliScalar P) (β : ZMod 2) : Prop :=
  _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.pauliPairGamma P z ≠ 0 ∨
    _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.fixedBinTrace P.model
      (a * (match W with
      | .X => _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.pauliRXBlock z
      | .Z => _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.pauliRZBlock z)) = β

/-- The Point/Variable consistency clause of `def:pauli-win-predicate`.
The check is gated by `gamma = 0` and only uses Variable 1 in the X basis or
Variable 5 in the Z basis.  Blueprint
`def:pauli-win-predicate`; paper origin
`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1126-1225`.
-/
def pauliPointVariableCondition (P : _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.AdmissibleParams) (W : _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.PauliKind)
    (z : _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.PauliSpace P) (j : Fin 9) (a : _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.PauliScalar P) (β : ZMod 2) : Prop :=
  _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.pauliPairGamma P z = 0 ∨
    (j = ⟨0, by decide⟩ ∧ W = .X ∧
        _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.fixedBinTrace P.model (a * _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.pauliRXBlock z) = β) ∨
    (j = ⟨4, by decide⟩ ∧ W = .Z ∧
        _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.fixedBinTrace P.model (a * _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.pauliRZBlock z) = β)

/-- The Pauli win predicate, with constructor-shape rejection.  This is
blueprint `def:pauli-win-predicate`,
paper origin `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1126-1225`.
-/
noncomputable def pauliWinPredicate (P : _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.AdmissibleParams) :
    _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.PauliQuestion P → _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.PauliQuestion P → _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.PauliAnswer P → _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.PauliAnswer P → Bool :=
  open Classical in
  fun (tA, xA) (tB, xB) a b =>
    if _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.validPauliAnswer tA a && _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.validPauliAnswer tB b then
      if tA = tB then
        decide (a = b)
      else
        match tA, tB, a, b with
      | .aline W, .point W', .alinePoly f, .value u =>
          if W = W' then decide (_root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.pauliAlinePointCondition P W xA xB f u) else true
      | .point W, .aline W', .value u, .alinePoly f =>
          if W = W' then decide (_root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.pauliAlinePointCondition P W xB xA f u) else true
      | .dline W, .point W', .dlinePoly f, .value u =>
          if W = W' then decide (_root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.pauliDlinePointCondition P W xA xB f u) else true
      | .point W, .dline W', .value u, .dlinePoly f =>
          if W = W' then decide (_root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.pauliDlinePointCondition P W xB xA f u) else true
      | .point W, .pauli W', .value u, .pauliOutcome h =>
          if W = W' then decide (_root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.pauliPointPauliCondition P W xA h u) else true
      | .pauli W, .point W', .pauliOutcome h, .value u =>
          if W = W' then decide (_root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.pauliPointPauliCondition P W xB h u) else true
      | .pairW W, .pair, .bit β, .pairBits bits =>
          decide (_root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.pauliPairCondition P W xA β bits)
      | .pair, .pairW W, .pairBits bits, .bit β =>
          decide (_root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.pauliPairCondition P W xB β bits)
      | .point W, .pairW W', .value u, .bit β =>
          if W = W' then decide (_root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.pauliPointPairCondition P W xB u β) else true
      | .pairW W, .point W', .bit β, .value u =>
          if W = W' then decide (_root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.pauliPointPairCondition P W xA u β) else true
      | .ms (.constraint i), .ms (.var j), .msTriple β, .bit γ =>
          if ∃ k : Fin 3, _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.msConstraintVars i k = j then
            decide (_root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.pauliPairGamma P xA = 0 ∨
              _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.msWinPredicate (.constraint i) (.var j) (.triple β) (.bit γ))
          else true
      | .ms (.var j), .ms (.constraint i), .bit γ, .msTriple β =>
          if ∃ k : Fin 3, _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.msConstraintVars i k = j then
            decide (_root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.pauliPairGamma P xB = 0 ∨
              _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.msWinPredicate (.var j) (.constraint i) (.bit γ) (.triple β))
          else true
      | .point W, .ms (.var j), .value u, .bit β =>
          decide (_root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.pauliPointVariableCondition P W xB j u β)
      | .ms (.var j), .point W, .bit β, .value u =>
          decide (_root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.pauliPointVariableCondition P W xA j u β)
        | _, _, _, _ => true
    else false

/-- The Pauli basis test determined by the question distribution
`pauliQuestionDistribution` and the win predicate `pauliWinPredicate`.  These
are `def:pauli-question-distribution` and `def:pauli-win-predicate` in
`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex`, with paper origin
`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:964-1225`.
-/
@[reducible] noncomputable def pauliBasisTest (P : _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.AdmissibleParams) : _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.Game where
  QuestionA := _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.PauliQuestion P
  QuestionB := _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.PauliQuestion P
  AnswerA := _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.PauliAnswer P
  AnswerB := _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.PauliAnswer P
  μ := _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.pauliQuestionDistribution P
  μ_prob := by
    classical
    letI : Nonempty _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.PauliEdge := _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.pauliEdge_nonempty
    exact _root_.LIDT.MIPStarRE.LDT.Distribution.IsProbability.map
      (_root_.LIDT.MIPStarRE.LDT.uniformDistribution_isProbability (_root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.PauliEdge × _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.PauliSpace P)) _
  decide := _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.pauliWinPredicate P

end

end MIPStarRE.QPBT

/-!
# Polynomial combination and restricted line distributions

This file contains the concrete definitions at the foundation of the
Chapter 15 combining argument.  A pair of bounded individual-degree
polynomials is embedded into the two coordinate blocks of an extended
polynomial.  On lines, explicit affine reparameterizations are composed with
coefficient-list polynomials.  The original-dimensional restricted line laws
are formed before decoding, while their field seed is still present.

## References

The combining map is blueprint
`def:combine-map`, with paper origin
`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:970-989`.
The restricted laws are blueprint `def:ith-restricted-line`,
with paper origin in the same source at lines 1038--1048.
-/

@[expose] public section

open scoped BigOperators

namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT

open LIDT.MIPStarRE.LDT
open LIDT.MIPStarRE.LDT.Preliminaries

noncomputable section

/-- The bounded individual-degree polynomial outcome used by the global
pair measurement.  This is the actual `polyFunc` subtype from
`def:polyfunc`, not a coefficient-box replacement. -/
noncomputable abbrev Poly (P : _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.AdmissibleParams) :=
  ↥(_root_.LIDT.MIPStarRE.LDT.Preliminaries.polyFunc P.m (_root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.PauliScalar P) P.d)

/-- Pairs of bounded polynomial representatives returned by the global
measurement in `lem:qld-4-7`. -/
noncomputable abbrev PolyPair (P : _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.AdmissibleParams) := _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.Poly P × _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.Poly P

/-- This equivalence decomposes the extended coordinate set into the `X` block,
    the `Z` block, and the two scalar coordinates.  It supports blueprint
`def:combine-map`, paper
`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:970-989`. -/
def finCombineEquiv (m : ℕ) :
    Fin (2 * m + 2) ≃ ((Fin m ⊕ Fin m) ⊕ Fin 2) :=
  (finCongr (by omega)).trans
    (finSumFinEquiv.symm.trans
      (Equiv.sumCongr finSumFinEquiv.symm (Equiv.refl (Fin 2))))

/-- Embed an `X`-block coordinate into the extended coordinate set. -/
def embX (m : ℕ) : Fin m → Fin (2 * m + 2) :=
  fun i => (_root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.finCombineEquiv m).symm (.inl (.inl i))

/-- Embed a `Z`-block coordinate into the extended coordinate set. -/
def embZ (m : ℕ) : Fin m → Fin (2 * m + 2) :=
  fun i => (_root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.finCombineEquiv m).symm (.inl (.inr i))

/-- The extended coordinate occupied by the scalar `alpha`. -/
def alphaVar (m : ℕ) : Fin (2 * m + 2) :=
  (_root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.finCombineEquiv m).symm (.inr 0)

/-- The extended coordinate occupied by the scalar `beta`. -/
def betaVar (m : ℕ) : Fin (2 * m + 2) :=
  (_root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.finCombineEquiv m).symm (.inr 1)

/-- Project an extended point onto its `X` coordinate block. -/
def projX {K : Type*} {m : ℕ} (u : Fin (2 * m + 2) → K) : Fin m → K :=
  fun i => u (_root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.embX m i)

/-- Project an extended point onto its `Z` coordinate block. -/
def projZ {K : Type*} {m : ℕ} (u : Fin (2 * m + 2) → K) : Fin m → K :=
  fun i => u (_root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.embZ m i)

/-- Combine two multivariate polynomials by the formula
`alpha * f(x) + beta * g(z)` from `def:combine-map`.

Blueprint `def:combine-map`; paper
`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:970-983`. -/
noncomputable def combinePoly {K : Type*} [CommSemiring K] {m : ℕ}
    (f g : MvPolynomial (Fin m) K) : MvPolynomial (Fin (2 * m + 2)) K :=
  MvPolynomial.X (_root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.alphaVar m) * MvPolynomial.rename (_root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.embX m) f +
    MvPolynomial.X (_root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.betaVar m) * MvPolynomial.rename (_root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.embZ m) g



/-- A fresh variable times an injectively renamed bounded polynomial retains
the same individual-degree bound.  This is a formalization-only auxiliary for
`def:combine-map`, paper
`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:970-983`. -/
private theorem x_mul_rename_mem_polyFunc {K : Type*} [CommSemiring K]
    {m n d : ℕ} (hd : 1 ≤ d) {e : Fin m → Fin n} (he : Function.Injective e)
    {a : Fin n} (ha : ∀ i, e i ≠ a) {p : MvPolynomial (Fin m) K}
    (hp : p ∈ _root_.LIDT.MIPStarRE.LDT.Preliminaries.polyFunc m K d) :
    MvPolynomial.X a * MvPolynomial.rename e p ∈ _root_.LIDT.MIPStarRE.LDT.Preliminaries.polyFunc n K d := by
  classical
  have hrenOutside {j : Fin n} (hj : j ∉ Set.range e) :
      (MvPolynomial.rename e p).degreeOf j = 0 := by
    apply Nat.le_zero.mp
    rw [MvPolynomial.degreeOf_le_iff]
    intro s hs
    rw [MvPolynomial.support_rename_of_injective he] at hs
    obtain ⟨t, _, rfl⟩ := Finset.mem_image.mp hs
    simp [Finsupp.mapDomain_notin_range _ _ hj]
  have hrenAll (j : Fin n) : (MvPolynomial.rename e p).degreeOf j ≤ d := by
    by_cases hj : j ∈ Set.range e
    · obtain ⟨i, rfl⟩ := hj
      rw [MvPolynomial.degreeOf_rename_of_injective he]
      exact _root_.LIDT.MIPStarRE.LDT.Preliminaries.degreeOf_le_of_mem_polyFunc hp i
    · rw [hrenOutside hj]
      exact Nat.zero_le d
  have haRange : a ∉ Set.range e := by
    rintro ⟨i, hi⟩
    exact ha i hi
  refine (MvPolynomial.mem_restrictDegree _ _ _).mpr ?_
  intro s hs j
  refine MvPolynomial.degreeOf_le_iff.mp ?_ s hs
  by_cases hj : j = a
  · subst j
    rw [mul_comm]
    exact (MvPolynomial.degreeOf_mul_X_self a _).trans (by
      rw [hrenOutside haRange]
      omega)
  · rw [mul_comm, MvPolynomial.degreeOf_mul_X_of_ne _ hj]
    exact hrenAll j

/-- The combining polynomial has individual degree at most `d` when
`hd : 1 ≤ d`.  The coordinate blocks are disjoint: `f` depends only on the
`x` variables and `g` only on the `z` variables, so multiplication by `alpha`
or `beta` preserves the degree bound on those old coordinates and gives degree
one only in the corresponding fresh coordinate.  Thus `hd` supplies exactly
the needed bound on the two fresh coordinates; no `d + 1` bound is introduced.
The statement is the well-definedness assertion in
blueprint
`def:combine-map`, with source context
`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:970-983` and the
boundary-hypothesis discussion in `docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_ld-dimension-divisibility.tex`.
-/
theorem combinePoly_mem_polyFunc {K : Type*} [CommSemiring K] {m d : ℕ}
    (hd : 1 ≤ d) {f g : MvPolynomial (Fin m) K}
    (hf : f ∈ _root_.LIDT.MIPStarRE.LDT.Preliminaries.polyFunc m K d) (hg : g ∈ _root_.LIDT.MIPStarRE.LDT.Preliminaries.polyFunc m K d) :
    _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.combinePoly f g ∈ _root_.LIDT.MIPStarRE.LDT.Preliminaries.polyFunc (2 * m + 2) K d := by
  have hsymm : Function.Injective (_root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.finCombineEquiv m).symm :=
    (_root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.finCombineEquiv m).symm.injective
  have hX : Function.Injective (_root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.embX m) := by
    intro i j hij
    simpa using hsymm hij
  have hZ : Function.Injective (_root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.embZ m) := by
    intro i j hij
    simpa using hsymm hij
  have haX : ∀ i, _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.embX m i ≠ _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.alphaVar m := by
    intro i hi
    simpa using hsymm hi
  have haZ : ∀ i, _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.embZ m i ≠ _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.betaVar m := by
    intro i hi
    simpa using hsymm hi
  exact Submodule.add_mem _ (x_mul_rename_mem_polyFunc hd hX haX hf)
    (x_mul_rename_mem_polyFunc hd hZ haZ hg)

/-- Evaluate one member of a global polynomial pair at a point, selecting the
component by Pauli basis.  This is formalization-only support for
`lem:qld-4-7`, paper
`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1267-1274`. -/
def evalAt {P : _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.AdmissibleParams} (W : _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.PauliKind)
    (u : Fin P.m → _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.PauliScalar P) (pair : _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.PolyPair P) : _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.PauliScalar P :=
  match W with
  | .X => MvPolynomial.eval u pair.1.1
  | .Z => MvPolynomial.eval u pair.2.1

/-- The univariate polynomial before coefficient extraction in
`combineLinePoly`.  The four first scalars describe the affine parameters on
the two projected lines; the last four are the affine `alpha` and `beta`
coordinates of the extended line. -/
noncomputable def combineLinePolynomial {K : Type*} [CommSemiring K] {c : ℕ}
    (aX bX aZ bZ uα vα uβ vβ : K)
    (f g : Fin (c + 1) → K) : Polynomial K :=
  (Polynomial.C uα + Polynomial.C vα * Polynomial.X) *
      (_root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.linePolynomialOfCoefficients f).comp
        (Polynomial.C aX + Polynomial.C bX * Polynomial.X) +
    (Polynomial.C uβ + Polynomial.C vβ * Polynomial.X) *
      (_root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.linePolynomialOfCoefficients g).comp
        (Polynomial.C aZ + Polynomial.C bZ * Polynomial.X)



/-- Combine two degree-`c` line polynomials using explicit affine
reparameterizations.  Coefficients through degree `c + 1` are extracted from
the genuine composed polynomial, so the definition has no incompatibility
fallback.

This is Equation `eq:combine-lines` in blueprint
`def:combine-map`, paper
`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:984-989`. -/
noncomputable def combineLinePoly {K : Type*} [CommSemiring K] {c : ℕ}
    (aX bX aZ bZ uα vα uβ vβ : K)
    (f g : Fin (c + 1) → K) : Fin (c + 1 + 1) → K :=
  fun i => (_root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.combineLinePolynomial aX bX aZ bZ uα vα uβ vβ f g).coeff i.val

/-- Compatibility of an extended line with two projected lines and their
explicit affine parameters. These data witness the projection-inclusion
condition preceding Equation `eq:combine-lines`. The theorem
`exists_isCombineLineCompatible_of_projection_mem` in `Combining/LinePolynomial.lean`
constructs them from that condition, including zero directions. Compatibility
alone does not make every coefficient answer a function on a singleton line;
see issue Dengnifer/MIPStarRE-QPBT-bak#695. -/
def IsCombineLineCompatible {K : Type*} [Field K] {m : ℕ}
    (u v : Fin (2 * m + 2) → K)
    (uX vX uZ vZ : Fin m → K)
    (aX bX aZ bZ uα vα uβ vβ : K) : Prop :=
  u (_root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.alphaVar m) = uα ∧ v (_root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.alphaVar m) = vα ∧
    u (_root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.betaVar m) = uβ ∧ v (_root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.betaVar m) = vβ ∧
    ∀ t : K,
      _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.projX (u + t • v) = uX + (aX + bX * t) • vX ∧
        _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.projZ (u + t • v) = uZ + (aZ + bZ * t) • vZ



/-- The seed event defining the `i`-th original-dimensional restricted line
law.  It is applied before the `LineDesc` decoder, since a geometric line does
not determine the retained seed. -/
def restrictedLineSeedEvent (L : _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.LdParams) (i : Fin L.m)
    (sample : _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.LdSpace L × _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.LdSpace L) : Prop :=
  _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.chiIndex L sample.1.seed = i

/-- Decidability of the pre-decoding seed event. -/
instance restrictedLineSeedEvent_decidablePred (L : _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.LdParams) (i : Fin L.m) :
    DecidablePred (_root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.restrictedLineSeedEvent L i) := by
  intro sample
  unfold _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.restrictedLineSeedEvent
  infer_instance

/-- Formalization-only auxiliary for `def:ith-restricted-line`: whenever a line
CL map keeps the shared scalar coordinate, the pre-decoding law it generates
against the point map gives positive mass to every coordinate-index event.  The
witness is the constant seed reconstructed from the index by
`seedOfIndexResidue`. -/
private theorem clDistribution_seedEvent_positive (L : _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.LdParams) (i : Fin L.m)
    (CL : _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.LdSpace L → _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.LdSpace L)
    (hseed : ∀ z : _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.LdSpace L, (CL z).seed = z.seed) :
    0 < ∑ sample ∈
        (_root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.clDistribution CL (_root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.ldPointCL L)).support.filter
          (_root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.restrictedLineSeedEvent L i),
      (_root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.clDistribution CL (_root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.ldPointCL L)).weight sample := by
  set s0 : _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.ScalarQ L := _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.seedOfIndexResidue L i ⟨0, L.seedFiberCard_pos⟩ with hs0
  set z0 : _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.LdSpace L := fun _ => s0 with hz0
  refine Finset.sum_pos'
    (fun a _ => (_root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.clDistribution CL (_root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.ldPointCL L)).nonnegative a)
    ⟨(CL z0, _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.ldPointCL L z0), Finset.mem_filter.mpr ⟨?_, ?_⟩, ?_⟩
  · refine Finset.mem_image.mpr ⟨z0, ?_, rfl⟩
    simp
  · change _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.chiIndex L (CL z0).seed = i
    rw [hseed]
    exact _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.chiIndex_seedOfIndexResidue L i _
  · refine Finset.sum_pos'
      (fun a _ => (_root_.LIDT.MIPStarRE.LDT.uniformDistribution (_root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.LdSpace L)).nonnegative a)
      ⟨z0, Finset.mem_filter.mpr ⟨?_, rfl⟩, ?_⟩
    · simp
    · simp only [_root_.LIDT.MIPStarRE.LDT.uniformDistribution, _root_.LIDT.MIPStarRE.LDT.Distribution.uniformOnFinset_weight,
        Finset.mem_univ, if_true]
      positivity

/-- The axis-line seed event has positive mass.  This named obligation makes
normalization in `restrictedALinePreDist` explicit.  It belongs to
blueprint
`def:ith-restricted-line`, paper
`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1038-1048`. -/
theorem restrictedALineSeedEvent_positive (L : _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.LdParams) (i : Fin L.m) :
    0 < ∑ sample ∈
        (_root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.clDistribution (_root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.ldALineCL L) (_root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.ldPointCL L)).support.filter
          (_root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.restrictedLineSeedEvent L i),
      (_root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.clDistribution (_root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.ldALineCL L) (_root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.ldPointCL L)).weight sample :=
  clDistribution_seedEvent_positive L i (_root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.ldALineCL L) fun _ => rfl

/-- The diagonal-line seed event has positive mass.  This is the corresponding
normalization obligation from blueprint `def:ith-restricted-line`; paper lines
1038--1048. -/
theorem restrictedDLineSeedEvent_positive (L : _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.LdParams) (i : Fin L.m) :
    0 < ∑ sample ∈
        (_root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.clDistribution (_root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.ldDLineCL L) (_root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.ldPointCL L)).support.filter
          (_root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.restrictedLineSeedEvent L i),
      (_root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.clDistribution (_root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.ldDLineCL L) (_root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.ldPointCL L)).weight sample :=
  clDistribution_seedEvent_positive L i (_root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.ldDLineCL L) fun _ => rfl

/-- The normalized pre-decoding axis law conditioned on coordinate `i`. -/
noncomputable def restrictedALinePreDist (L : _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.LdParams) (i : Fin L.m) :
    _root_.LIDT.MIPStarRE.LDT.Distribution (_root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.LdSpace L × _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.LdSpace L) :=
  _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.Distribution.restrict
    (_root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.clDistribution (_root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.ldALineCL L) (_root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.ldPointCL L))
    (_root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.restrictedLineSeedEvent L i)
    (_root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.restrictedALineSeedEvent_positive L i)

/-- The normalized pre-decoding diagonal law conditioned on coordinate `i`. -/
noncomputable def restrictedDLinePreDist (L : _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.LdParams) (i : Fin L.m) :
    _root_.LIDT.MIPStarRE.LDT.Distribution (_root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.LdSpace L × _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.LdSpace L) :=
  _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.Distribution.restrict
    (_root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.clDistribution (_root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.ldDLineCL L) (_root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.ldPointCL L))
    (_root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.restrictedLineSeedEvent L i)
    (_root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.restrictedDLineSeedEvent_positive L i)

/-- The `i`-th restricted refined axis-line distribution of blueprint
`def:ith-restricted-line`.  Restriction precedes decoding so the seed fiber is
represented faithfully.

**Formalization-only auxiliary:** the blueprint node is stated over the
refined, seed-bearing axis law, so this is an auxiliary restriction of that
refined law and not a formalization of a source distribution.  The paper
prose at
`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1038-1048`
describes the source restriction; identifying this law's push-forward with it
remains an open obligation recorded in
`docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_ld-dimension-divisibility.tex`, section
`sec:auxiliary-subline-scalars`. -/
noncomputable def restrictedALineDist (L : _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.LdParams) (i : Fin L.m) :
    _root_.LIDT.MIPStarRE.LDT.Distribution (_root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.LineDesc L × (Fin L.m → _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.ScalarQ L)) :=
  (_root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.restrictedALinePreDist L i).map fun sample =>
    (_root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.aLineDescOf L sample.1, sample.2.point)

/-- The `i`-th restricted refined diagonal-line distribution of blueprint
`def:ith-restricted-line`.  The decoded direction already has all coordinates
preceding `i` set to zero.

**Formalization-only auxiliary:** as for `restrictedALineDist`, the blueprint
node is stated over the refined, seed-bearing diagonal law.  The paper prose
at `references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1038-1048`
describes the source restriction; identifying this law's push-forward with it
remains an open obligation recorded in
`docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_ld-dimension-divisibility.tex`, section
`sec:auxiliary-subline-scalars`. -/
noncomputable def restrictedDLineDist (L : _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.LdParams) (i : Fin L.m) :
    _root_.LIDT.MIPStarRE.LDT.Distribution (_root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.LineDesc L × (Fin L.m → _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.ScalarQ L)) :=
  (_root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.restrictedDLinePreDist L i).map fun sample =>
    (_root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.dLineDescOf L sample.1, sample.2.point)





end

/-! # Polynomial decoding for Pauli extraction

This module provides the Chapter 16 decoder on the Chapter 15 bounded
polynomial representative type.  The generic retained-value decoder and its
specialization to polynomial representatives live in
`Algebra/LowDegreeCodeTheorems`; this module states the corresponding maps on
`Poly P` used in the extraction chapter.

## References

The decoder is blueprint `def:decoding-map`, with its extraction use in
blueprint `sec:separating` and paper
`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1419-1450`.
The restricted decoder identity and its encoding hypothesis are documented in
`docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_decoding-identity.tex:87-123`.
-/

@[expose] public section

open scoped BigOperators

namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT

open LIDT.MIPStarRE.LDT LIDT.MIPStarRE.LDT.Preliminaries

/-! ## Representative evaluation and decoding -/

/-- Evaluate the polynomial representative carried by `Poly P`.

This is polynomial evaluation on the source's `\ideg_{d,m}(\F_q)` carrier.  It
does not identify representatives that induce the same polynomial function. -/
noncomputable def evalPoly {P : _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.AdmissibleParams} (g : _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.Poly P)
    (x : Fin P.m → _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.PauliScalar P) : _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.PauliScalar P :=
  MvPolynomial.eval x g.1

/-- Decode a bounded polynomial while retaining only values in `H`.

This is the `H`-parameterized form of `def:decoding-map`; `decodeAt` remains
the decoding map for arbitrary functions.  The Boolean cube is embedded in
`PauliScalar P` by `cubeEmbed`. -/
noncomputable def decodeOn {P : _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.AdmissibleParams}
    (H : Finset (_root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.PauliScalar P)) (g : _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.Poly P) : _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.PauliRegister P :=
  _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.decodeAt H (fun x => _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.evalPoly g x)

/-- Full-field specialization of `decodeOn` used in Chapter 16.

The retained-value set is `Finset.univ`, so every field value is kept.  This
choice is the correction recorded in
`docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_decoding-identity.tex:87-123`. -/
noncomputable abbrev decodeOnUniv {P : _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.AdmissibleParams} (g : _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.Poly P) :
    _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.PauliRegister P :=
  _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.decodeOn (Finset.univ : Finset (_root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.PauliScalar P)) g

/-- The full-field decoder `\operatorname{Dec}_{\F_q}` on `Poly P`.

The map `decodeFqRep` has the same definition on arbitrary polynomial
representatives; `decodeFq` restricts its domain to the bounded-degree class
`Poly P`. -/
noncomputable abbrev decodeFq {P : _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.AdmissibleParams} (g : _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.Poly P) :
    _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.PauliRegister P :=
  _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.decodeOnUniv g

/-! ## The encoding image -/

/-- Membership of a multilinear encoding in the bounded representative class.

Each indicator factor has degree zero away from its own variable and degree at
most one in that variable, so the multilinear encoding has individual degree at
most one, and hence at most `P.d` using `P.hd`.  This is the degree
side-condition implicit in the source's `g_h` construction, not an extra
hypothesis of the decoding identity.  See blueprint
`def:low-degree-encoding`, and paper
`references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:832-897`. -/
theorem lowDegreeEncoding_mem_poly {P : _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.AdmissibleParams}
    (h : _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.PauliRegister P) :
    _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.lowDegreeEncoding h ∈
      _root_.LIDT.MIPStarRE.LDT.Preliminaries.polyFunc P.m (_root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.PauliScalar P) P.d := by
  rw [MvPolynomial.mem_restrictDegree]
  intro s hs i
  apply (MvPolynomial.monomial_le_degreeOf i hs).trans
  rw [_root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.lowDegreeEncoding]
  refine (MvPolynomial.degreeOf_sum_le i Finset.univ _).trans ?_
  refine Finset.sup_le fun y _ => ?_
  refine (show MvPolynomial.degreeOf i
      (h y • _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.indicatorPoly (K := _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.PauliScalar P) y) ≤
      MvPolynomial.degreeOf i (_root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.indicatorPoly (K := _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.PauliScalar P) y) from ?_).trans ?_
  · simpa only [MvPolynomial.smul_eq_C_mul] using
      MvPolynomial.degreeOf_C_mul_le (_root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.indicatorPoly (K := _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.PauliScalar P) y) i (h y)
  rw [_root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.indicatorPoly]
  refine (MvPolynomial.degreeOf_prod_le i Finset.univ _).trans ?_
  calc
    ∑ j, MvPolynomial.degreeOf i
        (if y j then
          (MvPolynomial.X j : MvPolynomial (Fin P.m) (_root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.PauliScalar P))
        else 1 - MvPolynomial.X j) ≤
        ∑ j, if i = j then 1 else 0 := by
      apply Finset.sum_le_sum
      intro j _
      split
      · exact le_of_eq (MvPolynomial.degreeOf_X i j)
      · exact (MvPolynomial.degreeOf_sub_le i 1 (MvPolynomial.X j)).trans_eq (by
          simp [MvPolynomial.degreeOf_X])
    _ = 1 := by simp
    _ ≤ P.d := P.hd

/-- The multilinear encoding as a bounded polynomial representative.

The individual-degree bound is supplied by `lowDegreeEncoding_mem_poly`. -/
noncomputable def encodingPoly {P : _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.AdmissibleParams} (h : _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.PauliRegister P) :
    _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.Poly P :=
  ⟨_root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.lowDegreeEncoding h, _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.lowDegreeEncoding_mem_poly h⟩

/-- A `Poly P` outcome is an encoding when its decoder reconstructs the same
underlying polynomial representative.

This is the explicit support restriction required by the corrected Chapter 16
decoding argument.  It is the `Poly` view of `IsEncodingRep`; no unrestricted
decoder/evaluation identity is asserted.  See
`docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_decoding-identity.tex:87-123`. -/
def IsEncoding {P : _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.AdmissibleParams} (g : _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.Poly P) : Prop :=
  _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.lowDegreeEncoding (_root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.decodeFq g) = g.1

/-! ## Decoder companions -/





/-- The full-field decoder is a left inverse to `encodingPoly`.

This is the identity `\operatorname{Dec}(g_h)=h` of
blueprint `lem:qld-decoder-linearity`, for
the full-field decoder specified at
`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1419-1420`.
The degree proof is separated into `lowDegreeEncoding_mem_poly`; no additional
encoding or interpolation hypothesis is introduced.  See
`docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_decoding-identity.tex:87-123`. -/
theorem decodeFq_lowDegreeEncoding {P : _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.AdmissibleParams}
    (h : _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.PauliRegister P) :
    _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.decodeFq (_root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.encodingPoly h) = h := by
  funext y
  simpa only [_root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.decodeFq, _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.decodeOnUniv, _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.decodeOn, _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.decodeAt, _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.evalPoly,
    _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.encodingPoly, _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.lowDegreeEnc, Finset.mem_univ, if_true] using
      congrFun
        (_root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.decodeAt_lowDegreeEnc
          (Finset.univ : Finset (_root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.PauliScalar P)) h
            (fun z => Finset.mem_univ (h z))) y



end MIPStarRE.QPBT

/-!
# Geometry for the directly indexed low-degree game

This module defines the parameters, line carrier, and line-point distributions
for the directly indexed low-degree game.

## References

The line-point distributions originate in
`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:243-272`.
The directly indexed repair is documented in
`docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_ld-dimension-divisibility.tex`.
-/

@[expose] public section

open scoped BigOperators

namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT

open LIDT.MIPStarRE.LDT
open LIDT.MIPStarRE.LDT.Preliminaries
open LIDT.MIPStarRE.Quantum

noncomputable section

/-- Parameters for the directly indexed low-degree game.  Unlike `LdParams`,
this directly indexed line-space construction has no divisibility field: its coordinate index is
sampled from `Fin m` rather than encoded by fibers of `chiIndex`.

This is the direct-index repair described in
`docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_ld-dimension-divisibility.tex`; it is not a second
definition of the source verifier game. -/
structure DirectLdParams where
  q : ℕ
  m : ℕ
  d : ℕ
  k : ℕ
  hm : 1 ≤ m
  hd : 1 ≤ d
  hk : 1 ≤ k
  hq : _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.IsAdmissibleSize q

/-- The canonical scalar model for directly indexed parameters. -/
@[reducible] noncomputable def DirectLdParams.model
    (D : _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.DirectLdParams) : _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.FixedFieldModel D.q :=
  _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.fixedFieldModel D.q D.hq

/-- The scalar field of a directly indexed low-degree game. -/
abbrev DirectScalarQ (D : _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.DirectLdParams) := D.model.K

/-- The first coordinate, available because directly indexed dimensions are
positive. -/
def DirectLdParams.firstIndex (D : _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.DirectLdParams) : Fin D.m :=
  ⟨0, lt_of_lt_of_le Nat.zero_lt_one D.hm⟩



/-- The direct game used at the extended dimension of the combining map.  Its
field, degree, and simultaneity parameters are inherited from `P`, while its
dimension is `2 * P.m + 2`; no divisibility assertion is introduced.

The construction has dimension `2 * P.m + 2` without requiring
`2 * P.m + 2 ∣ P.q`; it supplies the directly indexed line and coordinate
spaces used in the dimension-extension argument of blueprint `lem:qld-sublines`.
-/
@[reducible] def AdmissibleParams.extendedDirectLd (P : _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.AdmissibleParams) : _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.DirectLdParams where
  q := P.q
  m := 2 * P.m + 2
  d := P.d
  k := 1
  hm := by omega
  hd := P.hd
  hk := by decide
  hq := P.hq

/-- A common random sample for the directly indexed question distribution.
The point, coordinate index, and unrestricted direction are mutually uniform. -/
structure DirectLdSpace (D : _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.DirectLdParams) where
  point : Fin D.m → _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.DirectScalarQ D
  index : Fin D.m
  direction : Fin D.m → _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.DirectScalarQ D
  deriving DecidableEq, Fintype

instance instNonemptyDirectLdSpace (D : _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.DirectLdParams) : Nonempty (_root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.DirectLdSpace D) :=
  ⟨⟨0, D.firstIndex, 0⟩⟩

/-- Decompose a direct sample into its point and the remaining independent
coordinates. -/
def directLdSpacePointEquiv (D : _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.DirectLdParams) :
    _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.DirectLdSpace D ≃
      (Fin D.m → _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.DirectScalarQ D) ×
        (Fin D.m × (Fin D.m → _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.DirectScalarQ D)) where
  toFun sample := (sample.point, sample.index, sample.direction)
  invFun sample := ⟨sample.1, sample.2.1, sample.2.2⟩
  left_inv sample := by cases sample; rfl
  right_inv sample := by cases sample; rfl

/-- Decompose a direct sample into its stored index and the remaining
independent coordinates. -/
def directLdSpaceIndexEquiv (D : _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.DirectLdParams) :
    _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.DirectLdSpace D ≃
      Fin D.m ×
        ((Fin D.m → _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.DirectScalarQ D) ×
          (Fin D.m → _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.DirectScalarQ D)) where
  toFun sample := (sample.index, sample.point, sample.direction)
  invFun sample := ⟨sample.2.1, sample.1, sample.2.2⟩
  left_inv sample := by cases sample; rfl
  right_inv sample := by cases sample; rfl



/-- Zero the coordinates preceding the directly sampled prefix index. -/
def directPrefixProjection {D : _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.DirectLdParams} (i : Fin D.m)
    (v : Fin D.m → _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.DirectScalarQ D) : Fin D.m → _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.DirectScalarQ D :=
  fun j => if j.val < i.val then 0 else v j



/-- Canonical line descriptions whose coordinate index is stored directly.
Coordinates are numbered from zero, so `index = i` represents coordinate
`i + 1` in the paper. -/
inductive DirectLineDesc (D : _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.DirectLdParams) where
  | axis (base : Fin D.m → _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.DirectScalarQ D) (index : Fin D.m)
      (baseFixed : _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.lineRepMap (_root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.coordinateDirection index) base = base)
  | diagonal (base : Fin D.m → _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.DirectScalarQ D) (index : Fin D.m)
      (direction : Fin D.m → _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.DirectScalarQ D)
      (baseFixed : _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.lineRepMap direction base = base)
      (prefixZero : ∀ j : Fin D.m, j.val < index.val → direction j = 0)
  deriving DecidableEq

/-! ## Finite direct-line carrier -/

/-- A finite code for directly indexed lines, omitting only proof fields. -/
abbrev DirectLineDescCode (D : _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.DirectLdParams) :=
  ((Fin D.m → _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.DirectScalarQ D) × Fin D.m) ⊕
    ((Fin D.m → _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.DirectScalarQ D) × Fin D.m ×
      (Fin D.m → _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.DirectScalarQ D))

/-- Encode a directly indexed line by its tag and mathematical data. -/
def directLineDescCode (D : _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.DirectLdParams) :
    _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.DirectLineDesc D → _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.DirectLineDescCode D
  | .axis base index _ => .inl (base, index)
  | .diagonal base index direction _ _ => .inr (base, index, direction)

/-- The direct-line code is injective by proof irrelevance. -/
private theorem directLineDescCode_injective (D : _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.DirectLdParams) :
    Function.Injective (_root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.directLineDescCode D) := by
  intro line line' h
  cases line with
  | axis base index baseFixed =>
      cases line' with
      | axis base' index' baseFixed' =>
          simp only [_root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.directLineDescCode, Sum.inl.injEq, Prod.mk.injEq] at h
          rcases h with ⟨rfl, rfl⟩
          rfl
      | diagonal => simp [_root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.directLineDescCode] at h
  | diagonal base index direction baseFixed prefixZero =>
      cases line' with
      | axis => simp [_root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.directLineDescCode] at h
      | diagonal base' index' direction' baseFixed' prefixZero' =>
          simp only [_root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.directLineDescCode, Sum.inr.injEq, Prod.mk.injEq] at h
          rcases h with ⟨rfl, rfl, rfl⟩
          rfl

/-- Directly indexed line descriptions form a finite type. -/
noncomputable instance directLineDescFintype (D : _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.DirectLdParams) :
    Fintype (_root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.DirectLineDesc D) :=
  Fintype.ofInjective (_root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.directLineDescCode D) (by
    exact directLineDescCode_injective D)

/-- The kind of a directly indexed line. -/
def DirectLineDesc.kind {D : _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.DirectLdParams} : _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.DirectLineDesc D → _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.LineKind
  | .axis _ _ _ => .axis
  | .diagonal _ _ _ _ _ => .diagonal

/-- The coordinate index stored in a directly indexed line. -/
def DirectLineDesc.index {D : _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.DirectLdParams} : _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.DirectLineDesc D → Fin D.m
  | .axis _ index _ => index
  | .diagonal _ index _ _ _ => index

/-- The canonical base point of a directly indexed line. -/
def DirectLineDesc.base {D : _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.DirectLdParams} :
    _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.DirectLineDesc D → Fin D.m → _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.DirectScalarQ D
  | .axis base _ _ => base
  | .diagonal base _ _ _ _ => base

/-- The geometric direction of a directly indexed line. -/
def DirectLineDesc.direction {D : _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.DirectLdParams} (line : _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.DirectLineDesc D) :
    Fin D.m → _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.DirectScalarQ D :=
  match line with
  | .axis _ index _ => _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.coordinateDirection index
  | .diagonal _ _ direction _ _ => direction





/-- The point set represented by a directly indexed line. -/
noncomputable def DirectLineDesc.pointSet {D : _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.DirectLdParams}
    (line : _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.DirectLineDesc D) : Set (Fin D.m → _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.DirectScalarQ D) :=
  _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.linePoints line.base line.direction

/-- Turn a direct sample into its canonical axis-line description. -/
noncomputable def directALineDescOf (D : _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.DirectLdParams)
    (sample : _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.DirectLdSpace D) : _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.DirectLineDesc D :=
  let direction := _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.coordinateDirection sample.index
  let base := _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.lineRepMap direction sample.point
  .axis base sample.index (_root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.lineRepMap_apply_self direction sample.point)

/-- Turn a direct sample into its canonical diagonal-line description. -/
noncomputable def directDLineDescOf (D : _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.DirectLdParams)
    (sample : _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.DirectLdSpace D) : _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.DirectLineDesc D :=
  let direction := _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.directPrefixProjection sample.index sample.direction
  let base := _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.lineRepMap direction sample.point
  .diagonal base sample.index direction
    (_root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.lineRepMap_apply_self direction sample.point) (by
      intro j hj
      change _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.directPrefixProjection sample.index sample.direction j = 0
      rw [_root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.directPrefixProjection, if_pos hj])

/-- The axis-line/point law with a directly sampled coordinate index. -/
noncomputable def directALinePointDist (D : _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.DirectLdParams) :
    _root_.LIDT.MIPStarRE.LDT.Distribution (_root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.DirectLineDesc D × (Fin D.m → _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.DirectScalarQ D)) :=
  (_root_.LIDT.MIPStarRE.LDT.uniformDistribution (_root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.DirectLdSpace D)).map fun sample =>
    (_root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.directALineDescOf D sample, sample.point)

/-- The diagonal-line/point law with a directly sampled prefix index. -/
noncomputable def directDLinePointDist (D : _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.DirectLdParams) :
    _root_.LIDT.MIPStarRE.LDT.Distribution (_root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.DirectLineDesc D × (Fin D.m → _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.DirectScalarQ D)) :=
  (_root_.LIDT.MIPStarRE.LDT.uniformDistribution (_root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.DirectLdSpace D)).map fun sample =>
    (_root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.directDLineDescOf D sample, sample.point)

/-- The equal mixture of the directly indexed axis and diagonal line-point
laws.  This is the replacement for the otherwise undefined extended-dimension
instance used at paper
`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1020-1116`. -/
noncomputable def directLinePointDist (D : _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.DirectLdParams) :
    _root_.LIDT.MIPStarRE.LDT.Distribution (_root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.DirectLineDesc D × (Fin D.m → _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.DirectScalarQ D)) :=
  _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.Distribution.mix (1 / 2) (by norm_num) (by norm_num)
    (_root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.directALinePointDist D) (_root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.directDLinePointDist D)

















end

end MIPStarRE.QPBT

/-!
# The directly indexed low-degree game

This module defines polynomial evaluation, questions, answers, and the game
for the directly indexed low-degree interface.

## References

The underlying game is blueprint
`def:ld-game`, with source origin
`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
-/

@[expose] public section

open scoped BigOperators

namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT

open LIDT.MIPStarRE.LDT
open LIDT.MIPStarRE.LDT.Preliminaries
open LIDT.MIPStarRE.Quantum

noncomputable section

/-- Coefficient lists for a univariate polynomial of degree at most `c` in the
direct scalar field. -/
abbrev DirectDegPoly (D : _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.DirectLdParams) (c : ℕ) :=
  Fin (c + 1) → _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.DirectScalarQ D

/-- A direct line polynomial evaluates to `a` at `u` when `u` lies on the line
and every parameter presenting `u` gives value `a`.  The universal clause
keeps the zero-direction case explicit. -/
def DirectEvaluatesTo {D : _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.DirectLdParams} {c : ℕ} (line : _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.DirectLineDesc D)
    (f : _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.DirectDegPoly D c) (u : Fin D.m → _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.DirectScalarQ D)
    (a : _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.DirectScalarQ D) : Prop :=
  (∃ t : _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.DirectScalarQ D, u = line.base + t • line.direction) ∧
    ∀ t : _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.DirectScalarQ D, u = line.base + t • line.direction →
      _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.evalCoefficient f t = a

/-- Option-completed evaluation of a direct line polynomial.  `none` is an
explicit outcome when the point does not determine an evaluation; no field
value is used as a fallback. -/
noncomputable def directEvalOpt {D : _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.DirectLdParams} {c : ℕ}
    (line : _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.DirectLineDesc D) (u : Fin D.m → _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.DirectScalarQ D)
    (f : _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.DirectDegPoly D c) : Option (_root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.DirectScalarQ D) := by
  classical
  exact if h : ∃ a : _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.DirectScalarQ D, _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.DirectEvaluatesTo line f u a then
    some (Classical.choose h)
  else none

/-- The typed question alphabet of the directly indexed game. -/
abbrev DirectLdQuestion (D : _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.DirectLdParams) := _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.LdType × _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.DirectLdSpace D

/-- Canonicalize a common direct sample for one question type.  Irrelevant
coordinates are fixed, so point questions reveal no sampled line index and
axis-line questions reveal no diagonal direction. -/
noncomputable def directLdMap (D : _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.DirectLdParams) :
    _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.LdType → _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.DirectLdSpace D → _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.DirectLdSpace D
  | .point, sample => ⟨sample.point, D.firstIndex, 0⟩
  | .aline, sample =>
      let direction := _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.coordinateDirection sample.index
      ⟨_root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.lineRepMap direction sample.point, sample.index, 0⟩
  | .dline, sample =>
      let direction := _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.directPrefixProjection sample.index sample.direction
      ⟨_root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.lineRepMap direction sample.point, sample.index, direction⟩

/-- The directly indexed question distribution.  It has the same uniform
ordered type-pair branches as `ldQuestionDistribution`, but its common sample
contains an actual coordinate index rather than a field seed. -/
noncomputable def directLdQuestionDistribution (D : _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.DirectLdParams) :
    _root_.LIDT.MIPStarRE.LDT.Distribution (_root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.DirectLdQuestion D × _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.DirectLdQuestion D) :=
  (_root_.LIDT.MIPStarRE.LDT.uniformDistribution ((_root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.LdType × _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.LdType) × _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.DirectLdSpace D)).map fun sample =>
    ((sample.1.1, _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.directLdMap D sample.1.1 sample.2),
      (sample.1.2, _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.directLdMap D sample.1.2 sample.2))

/-- The directly indexed question law is probabilistic. -/
theorem directLdQuestionDistribution_isProbability (D : _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.DirectLdParams) :
    (_root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.directLdQuestionDistribution D).IsProbability := by
  exact (_root_.LIDT.MIPStarRE.LDT.uniformDistribution_isProbability
    ((_root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.LdType × _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.LdType) × _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.DirectLdSpace D)).map _

/-- The answer alphabet of the directly indexed game. -/
inductive DirectLdAnswer (D : _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.DirectLdParams) where
  | pointVals (a : Fin D.k → _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.DirectScalarQ D)
  | alinePolys (a : Fin D.k → Fin (D.d + 1) → _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.DirectScalarQ D)
  | dlinePolys (a : Fin D.k → Fin (D.m * D.d + 1) → _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.DirectScalarQ D)
  deriving DecidableEq

/-- A finite code for the directly indexed answer alphabet. -/
abbrev DirectLdAnswerCode (D : _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.DirectLdParams) :=
  (Fin D.k → _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.DirectScalarQ D) ⊕
    ((Fin D.k → Fin (D.d + 1) → _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.DirectScalarQ D) ⊕
      (Fin D.k → Fin (D.m * D.d + 1) → _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.DirectScalarQ D))

/-- The canonical code equivalence for `DirectLdAnswer`, sending point,
axis-line, and diagonal-line answers to the three summands. -/
noncomputable def directLdAnswerEquiv (D : _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.DirectLdParams) :
    _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.DirectLdAnswer D ≃ _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.DirectLdAnswerCode D where
  toFun
    | .pointVals a => .inl a
    | .alinePolys a => .inr (.inl a)
    | .dlinePolys a => .inr (.inr a)
  invFun
    | .inl a => .pointVals a
    | .inr (.inl a) => .alinePolys a
    | .inr (.inr a) => .dlinePolys a
  left_inv := by intro answer; cases answer <;> rfl
  right_inv := by
    intro answer
    rcases answer with a | a
    · rfl
    · rcases a with a | a <;> rfl

instance instInhabitedDirectLdAnswer (D : _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.DirectLdParams) : Inhabited (_root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.DirectLdAnswer D) :=
  ⟨.pointVals 0⟩

noncomputable instance instFintypeDirectLdAnswer (D : _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.DirectLdParams) :
    Fintype (_root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.DirectLdAnswer D) :=
  Fintype.ofEquiv (_root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.DirectLdAnswerCode D) (_root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.directLdAnswerEquiv D).symm

/-- Check that a direct-game answer has the constructor required by its
question type. -/
def validDirectLdAnswer {D : _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.DirectLdParams} (t : _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.LdType)
    (answer : _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.DirectLdAnswer D) : Bool :=
  match t, answer with
  | .point, .pointVals _ => true
  | .aline, .alinePolys _ => true
  | .dline, .dlinePolys _ => true
  | _, _ => false

/-- The directly indexed axis-line versus point acceptance relation. -/
def directAlinePointCondition (D : _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.DirectLdParams)
    (line point : _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.DirectLdSpace D)
    (f : Fin D.k → Fin (D.d + 1) → _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.DirectScalarQ D)
    (a : Fin D.k → _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.DirectScalarQ D) : Prop :=
  ∀ t : _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.DirectScalarQ D,
    point.point = line.point + t • _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.coordinateDirection line.index →
      ∀ j : Fin D.k, _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.evalCoefficient (f j) t = a j

/-- The directly indexed diagonal-line versus point acceptance relation. -/
def directDlinePointCondition (D : _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.DirectLdParams)
    (line point : _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.DirectLdSpace D)
    (f : Fin D.k → Fin (D.m * D.d + 1) → _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.DirectScalarQ D)
    (a : Fin D.k → _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.DirectScalarQ D) : Prop :=
  ∀ t : _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.DirectScalarQ D,
    point.point = line.point + t • line.direction →
      ∀ j : Fin D.k, _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.evalCoefficient (f j) t = a j

/-- The directly indexed low-degree win predicate.  It differs from
`ldWinPredicate` only by reading the coordinate index directly from each line
question. -/
noncomputable def directLdWinPredicate (D : _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.DirectLdParams) :
    _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.DirectLdQuestion D → _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.DirectLdQuestion D →
      _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.DirectLdAnswer D → _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.DirectLdAnswer D → Bool :=
  open Classical in
  fun (tA, xA) (tB, xB) a b =>
    if _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.validDirectLdAnswer tA a && _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.validDirectLdAnswer tB b then
      match tA, tB, a, b with
      | .point, .point, .pointVals u, .pointVals v => decide (u = v)
      | .aline, .point, .alinePolys f, .pointVals u =>
          decide (_root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.directAlinePointCondition D xA xB f u)
      | .point, .aline, .pointVals u, .alinePolys f =>
          decide (_root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.directAlinePointCondition D xB xA f u)
      | .dline, .point, .dlinePolys f, .pointVals u =>
          decide (_root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.directDlinePointCondition D xA xB f u)
      | .point, .dline, .pointVals u, .dlinePolys f =>
          decide (_root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.directDlinePointCondition D xB xA f u)
      | .aline, .aline, .alinePolys f, .alinePolys g => decide (f = g)
      | .dline, .dline, .dlinePolys f, .dlinePolys g => decide (f = g)
      | _, _, _, _ => true
    else false

/-- The directly indexed low-degree game at an arbitrary positive dimension.
It is an internal analysis game, not the conditionally linear verifier game
`ldGame`. -/
@[reducible] noncomputable def directLdGame (D : _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.DirectLdParams) : _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.Game where
  QuestionA := _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.DirectLdQuestion D
  QuestionB := _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.DirectLdQuestion D
  AnswerA := _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.DirectLdAnswer D
  AnswerB := _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.DirectLdAnswer D
  μ := _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.directLdQuestionDistribution D
  μ_prob := _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.directLdQuestionDistribution_isProbability D
  decide := _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.directLdWinPredicate D

/-- The canonical point question associated with a geometric point. -/
def directLdPointQuestionOf (D : _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.DirectLdParams)
    (u : Fin D.m → _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.DirectScalarQ D) : _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.DirectLdQuestion D :=
  (.point, ⟨u, D.firstIndex, 0⟩)

/-- Total point-answer relabeling used in the direct soundness conclusion.
Wrong-form answers are folded into the zero tuple, exactly as for
`ldPointValuesOrZero`. -/
def directLdPointValuesOrZero (D : _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.DirectLdParams) :
    _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.DirectLdAnswer D → Fin D.k → _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.DirectScalarQ D
  | .pointVals values => values
  | .alinePolys _ => 0
  | .dlinePolys _ => 0

/-- A simultaneous tuple of bounded polynomials for the directly indexed
game. -/
noncomputable abbrev DirectPolyTuple (D : _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.DirectLdParams) :=
  Fin D.k → _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.PolyIndex D.m (_root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.DirectScalarQ D) D.d

/-- A polynomial-tuple POVM for the directly indexed game. -/
noncomputable abbrev DirectPolyMeasTuple (D : _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.DirectLdParams) (ι : Type*)
    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] :=
  _root_.LIDT.MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement (_root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.DirectPolyTuple D) ι

/-- Evaluate every component of a direct polynomial tuple at a point. -/
def evalDirectPolyTupleAt {D : _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.DirectLdParams}
    (u : Fin D.m → _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.DirectScalarQ D) (g : _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.DirectPolyTuple D) :
    Fin D.k → _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.DirectScalarQ D :=
  fun j => MvPolynomial.eval u (g j).1

end

end MIPStarRE.QPBT

/-!
# Direct low-degree soundness for arbitrary strategies

This module transports directly indexed low-degree soundness at simultaneity
parameter `1` from projective strategies to arbitrary strategies. Both local
measurement families are dilated by the existing one-measurement Naimark
construction. The polynomial-tuple POVMs returned by projective soundness are
then compressed to the original player carriers at the distinguished ancillary
coordinate.

Ground-slice compression preserves all three consistency defects exactly, so
the error function and its universal constants are unchanged. The compressed
polynomial POVMs are not asserted to be projective.

## Main result

* `exists_direct_ld_soundness_of_k_eq_one_any_strategy` removes the projectivity
  premise from the formalization-only direct `k = 1` soundness route.

## References

The projective soundness input formalizes the shape of paper
`lem:ld-soundness`,
`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:413-458`.
The Naimark transport supports the first paragraph of the proof of paper
`lem:qld-4-7`,
`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1277-1289`.
This module is formalization-only support and does not claim completion of that lemma.
-/

@[expose] public section

open scoped BigOperators

namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT

open LIDT.MIPStarRE.LDT
open LIDT.MIPStarRE.LDT.Preliminaries
open LIDT.MIPStarRE.Quantum

noncomputable section

/-- Dilate every direct-game question measurement and pad the bipartite state
at the two distinguished `none` coordinates. -/
@[reducible]  def directLdNaimarkStrategy (D : _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.DirectLdParams)
    (S : _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.Strategy (_root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.directLdGame D)) : _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.Strategy (_root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.directLdGame D) :=
  _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.paddedStrategy S (none : Option (_root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.DirectLdAnswer D))
    (none : Option (_root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.DirectLdAnswer D))
    (fun question => _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.dilatedMeasurement (default : _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.DirectLdAnswer D) (S.A question))
    (fun question => _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.dilatedMeasurement (default : _root_.MIPStarRE.QPBT.DirectLdAnswer D) (S.B question))



















end

end MIPStarRE.QPBT
